en: The Jacobian philosophy has in common with the Kantian philosophy absolute finitude — the same in ideal form as formal knowledge, in real form as an absolute empiricism — and the integration of both through the faith that posits an absolute beyond.

But within this common sphere it forms the opposed pole to the Kantian philosophy, in which finitude and subjectivity has an objective form of the concept; the Jacobian philosophy, by contrast, makes subjectivity wholly subjective, into individuality.
This subjective element of the subjective again gains, as such, an inner life, and thereby seems to become capable of the beauty of feeling.
zh: 雅可比哲学与康德哲学共有的东西，是绝对的有限性——这种有限性在观念的形式中作为形式的知识，在实在的形式中作为绝对的经验主义——，以及通过那种设定一个绝对彼岸的信仰对两者的整合。
但在这个共同的领域之内，它构成了与康德哲学相对的另一极；在康德哲学里，有限性和主体性具有概念的一种客观形式；雅可比哲学则相反，把主体性完全弄成主观的，使之成为个体性。
这种主观东西之中的主观东西，作为这样的东西又重新获得一种内在的生命，并因此似乎变得能够拥有情感的美。

en: We consider first the subjectivity of knowledge, whose formal side Jacobi cognizes and purely sets forth immediately with consciousness and in abstraction; just as he positively asserts knowledge in this form alone and denies the objectivity of reason in knowledge, so too, where he polemicizes, he makes this knowledge count and contests the science of reason by means of it.
zh: 我们首先考察知识的主观性，即雅可比直接带着意识、在抽象中认识并纯粹地陈述出来的知识的形式方面；正如他肯定地只主张这种形式的知识，并否认理性在知识中的客观性，同样，在他论战的地方，他恰恰让这种知识生效，并借它来驳斥理性的科学。

en: That Jacobi everywhere knows only of formal knowledge, of an identity of the understanding whose content is filled by empirical knowledge, of a thinking to which reality in general is added in an incomprehensible way, is one of the few, or actually the only, point on which the Jacobian philosophy is objective and belongs to science; and this point is presented in distinct concepts.
My philosophy, says Jacobi (David Hume [1787], Vorr.

S. V), confines reason, considered for itself alone, to the mere capacity to perceive relations distinctly, i.e. to form the proposition of contradiction and to judge in accordance with it; but now I must admit that the affirmation of merely identical propositions alone is apodictic and carries an absolute certainty with it.
Likewise (Briefe über Spinoza, S. 215 f., 2.

Ausg., 1789151) ): conviction from grounds is a certainty from the second hand (the first hand is faith, of which later); grounds are only marks of similarity with a thing of which we are certain (namely through faith); the conviction which they bring about springs from comparison and can never be truly secure and perfect.

One of the five theses (ebenda S. 225) of the summary of his assertions is: we can demonstrate only similarities — for demonstration is progress in identical propositions —, and every proof presupposes something already proved, of which the principle is only revelation.152) Vgl. S. 421153): “The business of reason in general is progressive combination, and its speculative business is combination according to recognized laws of necessity ...

But the essential indeterminacy of human language and designation and the changeableness of sensory shapes almost universally lets these propositions acquire an external appearance, as if they asserted something more than the mere quicquid est, illud est, more than a mere factum that has been perceived, observed, compared, re-cognized and combined with other concepts.”
(See also S. 238, also David Hume, S. 94.154) )
zh: 雅可比处处只知道形式的知识，只知道一种知性同一性，其内容由经验来充实，只知道一种思维，实在性一般是以上一种不可理解的方式加到它上面的：这一点是雅可比哲学具有客观性、并且属于科学的少数几点之一，或者说其实就是唯一的一点；而这一点是用清晰的概念表述出来的。
我的哲学，雅可比说（《大卫·休谟》（David Hume）[1787]，Vorr.
S. V），把理性，就它自身单独来看，限制在单纯的能力上，即清晰地觉知关系，也就是构成矛盾命题并据此作判断；但现在我必须承认，只有对单纯同一的命题的肯定才是无可置疑的，并且带着一种绝对的确定性。
同样（《斯宾诺莎书信》（Briefe über Spinoza），S. 215 f.，2.
Ausg.，1789151)）：由根据而来的确信是一种第二手的确定性（第一手是信仰，后面再谈）；根据只是一事物与我们确信（即通过信仰而确信）的那个东西相似的标志；它们所产生的确信源自比较，永远不可能真正可靠而完满。
他那些主张的总纲的五个论题之一（同上，S. 225）是：我们只能证明相似的东西——因为证明就是在同一的命题中前进——，而任何证明都以某种已经证明了的东西为前提，它的原则只是启示。152) Vgl. S. 421153)：“理性一般的业务是渐进的联系，而它的思辨业务则是按照已被认识到的必然性规律的联系……
但人的语言和标记的本质上的不确定，以及感性形态的可变化，几乎到处都使这些命题获得一种外在的相貌，仿佛它们说出了比单纯的 quicquid est, illud est 更多的东西，比一个仅仅被知觉、被观察、被比较、被重新认出并与其他概念结合起来的事实更多的东西。”

en: The necessary counterpart to the proposition of identity is the proposition of ground, whether by it is understood the proposition of ground in general or the proposition of cause and effect or a union of the two according to Jacobi's distinctions (Briefe über Spinoza, S. 415155)); and as regards matter it is considered insofar as one proceeds from concepts to concepts, or from the concept to its reality, or from objective realities to others.
zh: 与同一性命题必然相对的是根据命题，不论这里所理解的是一般的根据命题，还是原因与结果的命题，还是按雅可比的区分（《斯宾诺莎书信》，S. 415155)）两者的结合；而就材料来看，它被考察，要看是从概念前进到概念，还是从概念前进到它的实在性，还是从客观的实在性前进到别的客观的实在性。

en: The older philosophical culture has laid down in the expression of the proposition of ground the testimony of its rational strivings, and its wavering between reason and reflection as well as its transition to the latter is very aptly indicated in the distinction which Jacobi makes between it as the logical proposition of ground and as the causal relation, and in which he makes both the way of understanding and the way of combating philosophy, which we intend to follow.

In the proposition of ground Jacobi recognizes its significance as the principle of rational cognition, totum parte prius esse necesse est (David Hume, S. 94)156); or the individual is determined only in the whole; it has its reality only in the absolute identity, which, insofar as what is distinguishable is posited in it, is absolute totality.

In one respect, says Jacobi, the totum parte prius esse necesse est is nothing other than idem est idem, but in another it is not, and with this — that these two respects are to be essentially distinguished and kept absolutely apart — this dogmatism of ground immediately begins.

For Jacobi grasps the proposition of ground as the pure proposition of contradiction and in this sense calls it logical — as abstract unity, to which it is of course necessary that the different be added as something empirical — and he distinguishes a causal relation, in which reflection is made on the heterogeneous, which is added to the identity of the concept and which is something empirically given, and asserts the causal relation, according to this peculiarity, as a concept of experience.

The way in which he demonstrates this (David Hume S. 99 f.157) and to which he appeals in Briefe über Spinoza, S. 415) is a remarkable piece of Lockean and Humean empiricism, into which an equally glaring piece of German analysing dogmatism, worse than in Mendelssohn's manner, has been kneaded, from which the world, next to Kant, cannot thank the gods enough for having been freed.

For in the proposition of ground and in the totality Jacobi misses the parts, and he must fetch these from somewhere besides the whole; or, as he grasps it, all the parts are really already united into a whole and present in it; but such an intuitive cognition of the parts out of the whole is only something subjective and incomplete, for the objective becoming and the succession are still missing, and on their account the causal relation must still be added to the totality.

Let one now hear the deduction of the, as Jacobi calls it, absolute necessity of the concept of cause and effect and of succession (David Hume, S. 111 ff.158)) in the following series of propositions:
zh: 较早的哲学教养在根据命题的表述中留下了它那些理性努力的见证，而它在理性与反思之间的摇摆以及向反思的过渡，非常贴切地表现在雅可比所作的那个区分里，他把根据命题区分为逻辑的根据命题和因果关系；他在这上面既走出理解哲学的路，也走出反对哲学的路，我们想沿着这条路走下去。
雅可比在根据命题中认识到它作为理性认识原则的意义：totum parte prius esse necesse est（《大卫·休谟》，S. 94）156)；或者说，单个的东西只有在整体中才得到规定；它只有在绝对同一性中才有它的实在性，而绝对同一性，只要其中有可区分的东西被设定，就是绝对总体性。
雅可比说，在一个方面，totum parte prius esse necesse est 不外是 idem est idem，在另一个方面却不是；而这种根据独断论恰恰就从这一点开始，即这两个方面必须本质上区分开来、绝对分开。
因为雅可比把根据命题理解为纯粹的矛盾命题，并在这个意义上把它叫作逻辑的——作为一种抽象的统一，当然必须让有差别的东西作为经验的东西加进来——，他还区分出一种因果关系，在这种关系中反思到那个加到概念同一性上来的、并且是经验地被给予的异质东西，并按照这一特点把因果关系断言为一个经验概念。
他论证这一点的方式（《大卫·休谟》S. 99 f.157)，以及他在《斯宾诺莎书信》S. 415 中援引的东西），是洛克式和休谟式经验主义的一个奇特部分，其中还揉进了一块同样刺眼的德国分析式独断论，比门德尔松那一套更糟；世界得以从中摆脱出来，除了康德之外，最该感谢诸神不过了。
因为在根据命题和总体性中，雅可比都缺了部分，他还得从整体之外的什么地方把这些部分取来；或者照他的理解，所有部分其实已经结合成一个整体并在其中存在；但这种从整体出发对部分的直观认识只是某种主观的、不完满的东西，因为还缺少客观的生成和接续，为了这二者的缘故，因果关系还必须加到总体性上来。
现在请听一听对——照雅可比的说法——原因与结果的概念以及接续的绝对必然性所作的演绎（《大卫·休谟》，S. 111 ff.158)），它由下面这一系列命题构成：

en: “For our human consciousness (and I may immediately add, for the consciousness of every finite being) there is, besides the sensing thing, also necessarily a real thing which is sensed.”
zh: “对我们的意识来说（我不妨马上补充一句：对每一个有限存在者的意识来说），除了能感觉的东西之外，还必然有一个被感觉到的现实的东西。”

en: “Where two created beings that are outside one another stand in such a relation to one another that the one works into the other, there is an extended being.”
zh: “凡是两个彼此外在的被创造的存在者彼此处于这样一种关系中，以致一个作用于另一个，那里就有一个广延的存在者。”

en: “We feel the manifold of our being bound together in a pure unity, which we call our I. — The inseparable in a being determines its individuality or makes it a real whole ...

Something somewhat analogous to individuality we perceive in bodily extension in general, in that the extended being as such can never be divided, but everywhere presents to the eyes the very same unity, which binds a multiplicity inseparably within itself.”
zh: “我们感到我们存在者中的杂多结合在一个纯粹的统一体里，这个统一体我们称为我们的我。——一个存在者中不可分离的东西规定着它的个体性，或者使它成为一个现实的整体……
某种在某种程度上与个体性类似的东西，我们在形体的广延中一般都能知觉到，因为广延的存在者作为这样的东西永远不能被分割，而是到处都呈现出同一个统一体，这个统一体把一种杂多不可分离地结合在自身之内。”

en: “Even if individuals have the capacity to work outside themselves ..., they must, if the effect is to follow, touch other beings mediately or immediately.”
zh: “即使各个个体有能力在自身之外起作用……，如果要产生效果，它们也必须间接地或直接地接触别的存在者。”

en: The immediate consequence of impenetrability in contact we call resistance. - Where, therefore, there is contact, there is impenetrability on both sides, and consequently also resistance, action and counter-action.
Both is the source of the successive and of time, of the representation of the same.
zh: 接触时不可入性的直接后果，我们称为阻力。——所以，凡有接触的地方，双方就都有不可入性，因而也就有阻力、作用和反作用。
这两者是相继的东西和时间的来源，也是它们的表象的来源。

en: From the presupposition, then, that individual beings that reveal themselves to themselves, which stand in community with one another, are present, this deduction of the concepts of extension, of cause and effect, and of succession has resulted, or the deduction of the absolute being of finitude, and at the same time it has thereby come out that these concepts must be common to all finite beings that reveal themselves to themselves and also have in things in themselves their object independent of the concept, and consequently a true objective meaning.
zh: 所以，从这样一个前提——存在着个别的、自己启示自己的、彼此处在共同体之中的本质——出发，就得出了这套关于延展、关于原因和结果、关于相继的概念的演绎，或者说有限东西的绝对存在的演绎；同时也就由此得出：这些概念必定是一切有限的、自己启示自己的本质所共有的，而且它们在自在之物中也拥有不依赖于概念的对象，因而拥有一种真正的客观含义。

en: Concepts of this kind, namely, which in every experience must be given completely and in such a way as the first, that without their objective element no object of a concept, and without their concept no cognition at all, would be possible, are called absolutely universal or necessary concepts, and the judgements and inferences arising from them, cognitions a priori.
zh: 这样一些概念，即必须在每一种经验中完整地、并且以这样的方式作为最初的东西被给予——以至于没有它们的客观东西，就没有任何概念的对象，没有它们的概念，就根本没有任何认识——，叫做绝对普遍的或必然的概念；而由它们产生的判断和推论，叫做先验认识。

en: We see that this deduction is meant to concern the causal relation in its whole extent, and that here something more cogent was to be delivered than the Kantian deduction.

But this Jacobian deduction deserves the name of a deduction so little that it cannot even be called an ordinary analysis of what is presupposed, namely of the concept of the community of individual things.

It is already something before which all speculation is horrified, namely that the absolute being of a human consciousness and of a sensing thing and of a sensed thing and of their community is simply presupposed straight out of the crudest empiricism; through superfluous middle terms they are finally analysed together into action and counter-action, and this is - here too the analysing gives out - the source of the successive.

One does not see at all what such a great feat is supposed to be good for; for already with the unanalysed absolute assumption of a sensing thing and of a thing that is sensed, all philosophy is struck off the field.

Remarkable is the difference of the presupposition and of the result from the result of the Kantian deduction of the category: according to Kant all these concepts of cause and effect, succession, etc. are absolutely restricted to appearance; the things in which these forms are objective, as well as a cognition of these objects, are absolutely nothing in themselves; the in-itself and reason are absolutely raised above these forms of finitude and kept pure of them - a result with which there remains to Kant the immortal merit of having made the beginning of a philosophy altogether.
But it is precisely in this nothing of finitude that Jacobi sees an absolute in-itself and with the dream of this weapon combats Spinoza's waking.
zh: 我们看到，这个演绎要涉及因果关系的全部范围，而这里本该拿出比康德的演绎更严密的东西。
但这个雅可比的演绎如此不配叫演绎，以至于它连对前提、即对个别事物的共同体这一概念的一种平常分析都算不上。
这已经是让一切思辨都害怕的事情：人的意识、感觉着的物、被感觉的物以及它们的共同体，其绝对存在竟直接从最粗陋的经验论里被预设下来；再借助多余的中间概念，它们最后被一并分析成作用和反作用，而这就是——分析在这里也到头了——相继的东西的来源。
人们根本看不出这样的高超把戏有什么用；因为只要未经分析地绝对假定一个感觉着的物和一个被感觉的物，一切哲学就已经被打下场了。
值得注意的是，这里的前提和结果与康德范畴演绎的结果之间的差别：按照康德，所有这些关于原因和结果、相继等等的概念，都绝对被限制在现象上；这些形式在其中是客观的那些物，以及对这样一些对象的认识，都绝对是自在的无；自在的东西和理性被绝对地提升到这些有限性的形式之上，并且对它们保持纯粹——有了这个结果，康德就保有不朽的功绩：他由此开创了哲学本身的开端。
但正是在这个有限性的无之中，雅可比看到了一个绝对的自在，并且用这件武器的梦去同斯宾诺莎的清醒作斗争。

en: If above we put the imperfection of the Kantian annihilation of the understanding in this, that he makes it with its forms indeed into something subjective, but in this shape nevertheless into something positive and absolute, then Jacobi, on the contrary, after he had so happily brought action and counter-action, succession, time, etc. out of the community of finite things, finds that one, 'in order that these fundamental concepts and judgements become independent of experience, need not make them into prejudices of the understanding, from which we must be healed by learning to recognize that they refer to nothing in itself, and consequently have no true objective meaning; for the fundamental concepts and judgements lose neither of their universality nor of their necessity when they are taken from what must be common to all experiences and lie at their ground.

They gain rather a far higher degree of unconditioned' (has the unconditioned degrees?) 'universality, if they hold not merely for the human being and his peculiar sensibility, but can be derived from the essence and the community of individual things altogether.

But if our senses teach us nothing at all about the qualities of things, nothing about their mutual relations and references, indeed not even that they are actually present in the transcendental understanding, and if our understanding relates merely to such a sensibility that presents nothing at all of the things themselves and is objectively absolutely empty, in order to procure thoroughly subjective forms for thoroughly subjective intuitions according to thoroughly subjective rules, then I am everything and outside me, in the proper sense, nothing.
And I, my everything, am in the end after all only an empty phantom of something, the form of a form, a spectre.

Such a system roots out all claims to cognition of the truth to the ground and leaves for the most important objects only such a blind faith, wholly empty of cognition, as has hitherto never yet been expected of human beings.'159)
zh: 如果说我们上面把康德消灭知性的不彻底处放在这一点上：他固然让知性连同它的形式成为某种主观的东西，但在这个形态下毕竟又把它弄成某种积极的、绝对的东西；那么雅可比则相反，在他如此幸运地把作用与反作用、相继、时间等等从有限事物的共同体中弄出来之后，他发现：人“为了使这些基本概念和判断不依赖于经验，并不需要把它们变成知性的偏见——我们必须从这些偏见中被治好，办法是学会认识到，它们并不关涉任何自在的东西，因而没有真正的客观含义；因为这些基本概念和判断，如果是从一切经验所共有、并且必然为它们奠基的东西里取来的，那么它们既不失去自己的普遍性，也不失去自己的必然性。
它们反而获得一种高得多的无条件的”（无条件者有程度吗？）“普遍性，如果它们不是仅仅对人及其特有的感性有效，而是能够从个别东西的本质和共同体本身推导出来。
但如果我们的感官根本不告诉我们物的性状，不告诉我们它们相互的关联和关系，甚至不告诉我们它们在先验知性中现实地存在着；如果我们的知性只是与这样一种根本不呈现物自身的、在客观上完全空洞的感性相关，为的是按照完全主观的规则，给完全主观的直观弄出完全主观的形式——那么我就是一切，而在我之外，就本来的意义说，什么也不是。
而自我，我的一切，到头来毕竟也只是某个东西的空洞幻影，是形式的形式，是一个幽灵。
这样一个体系把对真理认识的一切要求连根拔掉，对最重要的对象只留下一种盲目的、完全没有任何认识的信仰，而人们至今还从没有向人要求过这样的信仰。”159)

en: It is here to be distinguished that only in this, that Kant misrecognizes the rational as such, lies his faith empty of cognition, but not in his great theory that the understanding cognizes nothing in itself.

What, on the other hand, Jacobi enriches human cognition with are things such as the absolute being of finite things and of their community, of time and of succession and of the causal connection, which (David Hume S. 119) also have in things in themselves their object independent of the concept.

But that such absolutes of objective finitude [would be] negated and cognized as nothing in itself, and consistently likewise the subjective finitude, the sensible and reflectively thinking I, my everything, would also be only an empty phantom of something in itself, that my finite everything perishes before reason just as well as the everything of the objective finite - that is for Jacobi the dreadful and horrifying thing; the abhorrence of the annihilation of the finite is fixed just as much as the correlate, the absolute certainty of the finite, and will prove itself throughout as the fundamental character of the Jacobian philosophy.

One could at first take it for an improvement of the Kantian deduction that Jacobi conceives succession and causal connection as relation altogether, namely as a merely relative relation restricted to finite things, and in the deduction of the same, if what was cited above is otherwise a deduction, proceeds not merely as Kant does from a conscious but at the same time from an unconscious understanding; but, not to mention that the relation considered subjectively, or the conscious understanding, and the very same considered objectively, or as understanding, the relation of things, stand wholly independently and dualistically side by side, and that Kant has the relation at least absolutely only as one, without a difference of a subjective understanding and a particular objective one and - even if we must conceive the understanding in Kant as something subjective - yet no external, alien relation of things, and thus only one understanding, in which at least the formal element of philosophy is expressed - the most important result of Kant is always that these relations of the finite (whether they be relations of the subjective alone or relations of things at the same time) are nothing in themselves, that cognition according to them is only a cognition of appearances (although it is not to be gone beyond, and it therefore becomes absolute).

The a priori element of the Jacobian relations, on the other hand, consists in this, that they also belong to things in themselves, i.e. that the finite things, the sensing thing and besides it the actual thing which is sensed, are things in themselves, and the relations of such things, succession, causal connection, resistance, etc., are true relations of reason or ideas, so that therefore the apparent improvement, according to which the relations would be not merely something subjective of the conscious understanding but also something objective, unconscious, in truth constitutes an absolute dogmatism and an elevation of the finite to an in-itself.
zh: 这里要区分清楚：康德那种没有认识的信仰，只在于他把理性的东西本身认错了，而不在于他那个伟大的理论，即知性不认识任何自在的东西。
相反，雅可比用来丰富人的认识的东西，是有限事物及其共同体、时间、相继和因果关联的绝对存在这样一些东西；这些东西（David Hume S. 119）也在自在之物中拥有不依赖于概念的对象。

但是，这样一些客观有限性的绝对者[会]被否定、被认识到是自在的无，而且顺理成章地，主观的有限性、感性的和反思着思维的自我、我的一切，也会只是某个东西在自在中的空洞幻影；我的有限的一切在理性面前同样要归于毁灭，正如客观有限东西的一切要归于毁灭——这对雅可比来说才是可怕而令人毛骨悚然的事情；对有限东西之毁灭的憎恶，与和它相应的东西、即有限东西的绝对确定性，同样是被固定下来的，而且将彻底表明自己是雅可比哲学的基本特征。

人们最初可以把这一点看作对康德演绎的改进：雅可比把相继和因果关联领会为一般的关系，即领会为一种纯粹相对的、被限制在有限事物上的关系，并且在它们的演绎中——如果上面引述的东西真算得上一种演绎的话——不只是像康德那样从一个有意识的知性出发，而是同时从一个无意识的知性出发；然而，且不说关系从主观方面看、即有意识的知性，与同一个东西从客观方面看、即作为知性、作为事物的关系，是完全独立地、二元地并列共存的，也不说康德至少把关系绝对地只当作一种关系，没有主观知性与一个特殊的客观知性的区别，并且——即使我们也必须把康德那里的知性领会为某种主观的东西——毕竟没有一种外在的、异己的事物关系，因而只有一个知性，其中至少表达出了哲学的形式东西；——那么，康德最重要的结果始终是：有限东西的这些关系（无论是仅仅主观东西的关系，还是同时是事物的关系）都不是自在的什么，按照它们去认识只是一种对现象的认识（尽管不该超出这个范围，因此它就变成绝对的）。
相反，雅可比那些关系的先验性在于：它们也属于自在之物，也就是说，有限事物、感觉着的物以及在此之外被感觉到的现实的物，都是自在之物，而这类事物的关系，即相继、因果关联、阻力等等，是真正的理性关系或观念；因此，那个表面上的改进——按照它，这些关系不只是有意识知性的某种主观东西，而且也是某种客观的、无意识的东西——实际上构成了一种绝对的独断论，并且把有限东西提升为自在。

en: The application, now, which Jacobi makes to Spinoza's system of the grounding of the absolute being of the finite, which resulted from the important distinction of the proposition of ground and causality, has two forms: on the one hand, that the concept of succession is lacking in it, on the other hand, that it is at bottom nevertheless present, but in the absurdity of an eternal time.
zh: 雅可比把对有限东西绝对存在的论证应用于斯宾诺莎的体系——这一论证是从根据命题与因果性的重要区分中得出的——这种应用有两种形式：一种说斯宾诺莎体系里缺少相继的概念，另一种说它其实还是有的，只是在一种永恒时间的荒谬形态里。

en: As regards the lack of time, Jacobi takes up Spinoza's philosophy in such a way that Spinoza is supposed to have wanted to bring about a natural explanation of the determinate being of finite and successive things.

But in that he cognized things according to the concept of reason as present at the same time - for in the concept of reason there is no before and after, but everything necessarily and at the same time - and the universe in an eternal manner, he is supposed to have committed the error of taking the proposition of ground wholly and solely logically, and thereby of positing not an objective and actual but only a subjective and ideal succession, which could not even once be present ideally if an actual succession in the subject that produces it in the thought did not lie at its ground; in the logical proposition of ground, succession itself is supposed to be the incomprehensible.160)
zh: 就缺少时间这一点来说，雅可比把斯宾诺莎的哲学理解为：斯宾诺莎想要对有限的和相继的事物的定在作出一种自然的解释。

但是，由于他按照理性概念把事物认作同时存在的——因为在理性概念里没有在先和在后，而是一切都必然地、同时地存在——并且以永恒的方式认识宇宙，他就犯了这样的错误：把根据命题完全只当作逻辑的命题来理解，因此设定的不是一种客观的、现实的相继，而只是一种主观的、观念的相继；而这种相继如果不是以那个在思想中产生它的主体里的一种现实的相继为基础，就甚至不可能作为观念的相继而存在；在逻辑的根据命题里，相继本身据说就是不可理解的东西。160)

en: There is nothing to be said about such a psychological reminder, that a subjective and ideal succession presupposes an actual succession in the subject.

Thereby in part nothing at all is said, in part something false, since namely the ideal succession refers to Spinoza's mathematical similes, of which there will be talk afterwards, and according to its truth can be something real only because it is the absolute at-once of the totality and no succession at all.

But this absolute at-once of the totality and the cognition of things as they are in a not temporal but eternal manner, Jacobi ascribes to the proposition of ground and to the neglect of the law of causality, and indeed the same understood in such a way that time is posited in it.

And that this causality and time may not be neglected - of this the absolute ground lies in the fact that according to Jacobi time is in itself and absolute; and the proposition of ground or the totality is therefore called logical by Jacobi, because in it cause and effect are posited at the same time and no time is posited.

But if one did not forget the proposition of causality and its difference from the proposition of ground, then one would sit immovably fixed in time161); and this is with Jacobi an absolute requirement.

If Jacobi so earnestly admonishes us not to forget his distinctions, because through the concept of reason, in which there is no before and after, but everything necessarily and at the same time, the misfortune is supposed to arise that in the highest idea, in the idea of the eternal, finitude and time and succession get lost, then such a warning truly resembles the well-known waving of the honest imperial-city guard, who called out to the advancing and firing enemy not to shoot, because there could be a misfortune - as if such a misfortune were not precisely what one was aiming at.
zh: 对于这样一种心理学的提醒，即主观的、观念的相继预设了主体里的一种现实的相继，没有什么可说的。
这样一来，一半是什么也没说，一半是说错了；因为这个观念的相继指的是斯宾诺莎的那些数学比喻——后面还要谈到——而且就它的真理来说，它之所以能是某种实在的东西，仅仅因为它是总体性的绝对同时，根本不是相继。
但是，总体性的这种绝对同时，以及对事物就其非时间性的、永恒的存在方式而有的认识，雅可比把它们归给根据命题和对因果律的忽视，而且是把这同一个东西理解为：时间被设定在它之中。
至于这种因果性和时间不可以被忽视，其绝对的根据就在于：按雅可比，时间是自在的、绝对的；而根据命题或总体性在雅可比那里之所以叫做逻辑的，是因为在它之中原因和结果是同时被设定的，没有时间被设定。
可是，如果人们不忘记因果性命题及其与根据命题的区别，那么人就会一动不动地卡在时间里161)；而这在雅可比那里是绝对的要求。
如果雅可比如此郑重地告诫人们不要忘记他的那些区分，理由是：通过理性概念——在它之中没有在先和在后，而是一切都必然地、同时地存在——会产生这样的不幸，即在最高的观念里、在永恒者的观念里，有限性、时间和相继都丢失了；那么这样一种劝阻，就真像那个老实巴交的帝国城市卫兵人所共知的那种挥手示意：他冲正在逼近并开火的敌人喊，别开枪，因为可能会出不幸——好像这样的不幸不正是人们所谋求的东西似的。

en: From the fact that in the concept of reason everything is at once, Jacobi drew the simple and correct conclusion that we are thereby compelled to assume that in nature everything is at once, and that what we call succession is a mere appearance.

How Jacobi could take any credit for his discovery of this paradoxical proposition, as he calls it - at which he is astonished that Mendelssohn was the first to have found it, and to have admitted it without hesitation (succession and duration, says Mendelssohn162), are very well necessary determinations of limited thinking), whereas Jacobi, on the other hand, had to defend it against the other philosophers (!), to whom he submitted it - and which he put forward not in earnest, but only as a necessary consequence of the proposition of ground163) - as a proposition that did not belong to Spinoza, is really incomprehensible.
Could Jacobi, Spinoza's commentator, then perhaps mean of Spinoza that he had placed time in God, and that according to him time belongs only to the natura naturata?

We shall really see at once that, after Jacobi had concluded that Spinoza must properly declare time to be mere appearance, he nevertheless finds time in Spinoza, and indeed in the absurdity of an eternal time.

If [Spinoza], in the few passages where he incidentally comes to speak of this subordinate form of succession - for example in the second book of the Ethics and in the Letters - and isolates the infinite series of finite things under this form of abstraction, uses not thinking but imagining of it, and calls it distinctly enough an auxilium imaginationis, then Jacobi surely knew Spinoza's distinction between intellectus and imaginatio.

The absolute at-once, and that God is not the transient but the eternal cause of things, and that things are outside God, hence also in time, and that time itself is nothing in itself - every line in Spinoza's system makes the proposition that time and succession are mere appearance such a triviality that not the least trace of novelty and paradox is to be seen in it.

Jacobi cites (Letters on Spinoza, p. 409)164) that it was Spinoza's conviction that everything must be considered only secundum modum, quo a rebus aeternis fluit, and that time, measure and number are, as ways of representing separated from this modus, consequently the essence of the imagination.
How then should that proposition not belong to Spinoza?

For Jacobi that proposition is so paradoxical that he not only did not assert it in earnest, but out of this most finite form of finitude makes outright something absolute, and grounds the entire refutation of Spinoza on the claim that the latter did not conceive the proposition of ground in such a way that time is in it, and explains Spinoza's deception about philosophy from this, just as he himself, for the sake of this finitude, recognizes the undertaking of reason as impossible and contingent.
zh: 雅可比从“在理性概念里一切都同时存在”这一点得出了那个简单而正确的结论：我们因此不得不假定，在自然里一切都同时存在，而我们称为相继的东西只是一种现象。

雅可比把自己发现这个他称为悖论的命题——他对门德尔松竟是第一个毫不迟疑地发现它、并且承认它的人（门德尔松说162）：相继和持续是很可以作为有限思维的必然规定的）感到惊讶，而雅可比却要把它拿去对付他向其陈述这一命题的其他哲学家（！），为之辩护——并且他提出这个命题并不是当真的，只是把它当作根据命题的一个必然后果163）——他竟能因为这个发现而自鸣得意，把它当作一个不属于斯宾诺莎的命题，这实在是不可理解的。
雅可比这位斯宾诺莎的注释者，难道会认为斯宾诺莎把时间放进了上帝之中，而按照斯宾诺莎，时间也只属于被自然化的自然吗？
我们真的马上就会看到，在雅可比推论出斯宾诺莎本应把时间解释为单纯的现象之后，他却又在斯宾诺莎那里找到了时间，而且是在一种永恒的时间这种荒谬形式中找到的。
如果说[斯宾诺莎]在他偶尔谈到相继这一从属形式的少数地方——例如在《伦理学》第二卷和书信中——并且在这种抽象形式下把有限事物的无限系列分离出来时，用的不是思维而是想象，而且说得足够明确，称它为 auxilium imaginationis（想象的帮助），那么雅可比当然是熟悉斯宾诺莎对 intellectus（知性）和 imaginatio（想象）的区分的。
那个绝对的“同时”，以及上帝不是事物转瞬即逝的原因而是永恒的原因、事物在上帝之外因而也在时间之中、而时间本身自在什么也不是——斯宾诺莎体系里的每一行都把“时间和相继只是现象”这一命题变成这样一种老生常谈，以致在其中看不到半点新奇和悖论的痕迹。
雅可比引证（《论斯宾诺莎的书信》，第 409 页）164）说，斯宾诺莎的信念是：一切都只能 secundum modum, quo a rebus aeternis fluit（按照它们从永恒事物流出的方式）来考察，而时间、度量和数则是与这种方式分离开的表象方式，因而是想象的本质。
那么，这个命题怎么就不该属于斯宾诺莎呢？
在雅可比看来，那个命题是如此悖谬，以致他不但没有当真主张过它，反而从这种最有限制的有限性形式中径直造出了某种绝对的东西，并且把对斯宾诺莎的全部反驳都建立在这一点上：斯宾诺莎没有把根据命题把握成时间就在其中，又把斯宾诺莎对哲学的迷误由此解释一番，正如他自己为了这种有限性而把理性的这一事业认作不可能的和偶然的。

en: But Jacobi really does find the inconsistency in Spinoza, that he posited time as something in itself; he finds in the infinite series of individual things, of which one after (!) the other had come to actuality, at bottom (where is this ground?) an eternal time, an infinite finitude, and this absurd assertion could not be set aside by any mathematical figure, but here Spinoza had let himself be deceived by his imagination.165)
zh: 但雅可比确实在斯宾诺莎那里发现了不一致：斯宾诺莎把时间设定为自在的东西；他在单个事物的无限系列中——这些事物是一个（！）接着另一个获得现实性的——归根到底（这个根据在哪里？）发现了一种永恒的时间、一种无限的有限性，而这个荒谬的主张无法靠任何数学图形排除掉，斯宾诺莎在这里是让他的想象力骗了自己。165）

en: We want to shed light first on Spinoza's infinite series of finite things, then on the eternal time that Jacobi makes out of it, and on the inadmissibility of the mathematical similes.
zh: 我们要先照亮斯宾诺莎的有限事物的无限系列，然后照亮雅可比由此造出的永恒的时间，再照亮那些数学比喻的不成立。

en: It is precisely the infinitum actu, which Spinoza elucidates in the 29th Letter166), to which Jacobi also pays attention, and of which Spinoza says that those who mix the things of the imagination - number, measure and time - with the things themselves, because they do not know the true nature of things, deny it167), that Jacobi mixes with the infinite of the imagination.
The infinite Spinoza defines (Ethics, P. I, Pr.
VIII, Sch.

I) as the absolute affirmation of the existence of some nature, the finite on the contrary as a partial negation.168) This simple determination therefore makes the infinite into the absolute, self-same, indivisible true concept, which includes the particular or finite according to its essence at the same time within itself and is one and indivisible, and this infinity, in which nothing is negated and determined, Spinoza calls the infinity of the understanding; it is the infinity of substance, and its cognition [is] the intellectual intuition, in which, as intuitive knowledge, the particular and finite is not, as in the empty concept and the infinity of abstraction, excluded and opposed, and this infinite is the idea itself.

By contrast, the infinite of the imagination arises in a quite different way, namely, as Spinoza expresses himself, the existence and duration of the modorum we can, if we look not at the order of nature itself but at its particular essence, insofar as its concept is not the concept of substance itself, determine and divide at will, and if we grasp the quantity abstractly from substance, but the duration from the mode according to which it flows from eternal things, then time and measure arise for us.169) Or through what Spinoza calls imagination, or generally through reflection, the finite is first posited, is negated in part, and this in-part negated, posited for itself and opposed to the in-itself not negated, absolutely affirmative, makes this infinite itself into an in-part negated or into an abstraction, into the Kantian pure reason and infinity, in that the same is brought into opposition - and as the absolute identity of both, the eternal is to be posited, in which this infinite and that finite are again annihilated according to their opposition.

But it is another matter when the abstracted, finite or infinite remains what it is, and each is to be taken up into the form of the opposed; here the one is determined as not being what the other is, and each as posited and not posited, as this determinate one being and as being another, and such a law runs out into the empirical infinity.

Duration, as posited solely through imagination, is a moment of time, a finite thing, and, fixed as such, an in-part negated thing, at the same time determined in and for itself as being another; this other, which likewise receives its actuality through the imagination, is likewise another.
This negation, which remains what it is, made positive through the imagination, gives the empirically infinite, i.e. an absolute, unresolved contradiction.
zh: 正是这个 infinitum actu（现实中的无限），斯宾诺莎在第 29 封信166）里作了阐明——雅可比也注意到这封信——斯宾诺莎说，那些把想象力的事物即数、度量和时间同事物本身混在一起的人，因为不认识事物的真正本性，就否认它167），而雅可比恰恰把它与想象力的无限混在了一起。
斯宾诺莎把无限定义为（《伦理学》第一部分，命题
第八，附释

一）某一本性存在的绝对肯定，相反把有限定义为部分的否定。168）所以这个单纯的规定就把无限弄成了绝对的、自身同一的、不可分的真概念，这个概念按其本质同时把特殊者或有限者包含在自身之内，并且是唯一的和不可分的，而这种其中没有任何东西被否定和被规定的无限性，斯宾诺莎称为知性的无限性；它是实体的无限性，而对它的认识[是]智性直观，在这种直观认识里，并不像在空洞的概念和抽象的无限性里那样，把特殊者和有限者排除出去并与之对立，而这个无限者就是观念本身。

相反，想象力的无限是以完全另一种方式产生的，就是说，用斯宾诺莎自己的话：诸样式（modorum）的存在和持续，如果我们看的不是自然本身的秩序，而是它们的特殊本质——只要它们的概念不是实体自身的概念——我们就能任意加以规定和划分，而如果我们把量从实体抽象出来理解、把持续则从样式借以从永恒事物流出的那种方式抽象出来理解，那么就产生了时间与度量。169）或者说，通过斯宾诺莎称为想象力的东西，或者一般地说通过反思，才设定了有限的东西，作了部分的否定，而这个被部分否定的东西，被设定为自为的、并与那个自在并非被否定者、即绝对肯定者相对立，就使这个无限者本身也成了一个被部分否定者或一个抽象，成了康德式的纯粹理性和无限性，因为它被带进了对立之中——而作为两者的绝对同一性，则要设定永恒者，在这个永恒者中，这个无限者和那个有限者又按照它们的对立被扬弃掉了。
但另一种情形是：被抽象出来的东西、有限者或无限者仍然是它之所是，而每一个都应被纳入对立面的形式之中；在这里，这一个被规定为不是另一个所是的东西，而每一个都被规定为既被设定又未被设定，既作为这个被规定者而存在，又作为存在者的另一个；而这样一种法则一直延伸到经验性的无限之中。
持续既然仅仅通过想象被设定，就是一个时间环节、一个有限者，而作为这样的东西被固定下来，就是一个被部分否定者，同时自在自为地被规定为存在着的另一个；这个另一个，同样通过想象获得它的现实性，也同样是另一个。
这个仍然是它之所是的否定，通过想象被弄成肯定的，就给出经验性的无限，也就是一个绝对的、未被消解的矛盾。

en: This empirical infinity, which is posited only insofar as individual things are posited (Ethics, P. I, Pr.

XXVIII) - individual things, which Jacobi on the contrary above in his deduction absolutely posited as a sensing thing and as a thing that is sensed, but which are in themselves absolutely nothing - Jacobi charges Spinoza with without further ado, although no philosopher was further removed than he from assuming such a thing; for with the not-being-in-itself of finite things, such empirical infinity and time fall away immediately.

Jacobi says Spinoza assures us that it lies merely in our imagination if we represent to ourselves an infinite series of successive individual things, objectively and really springing from one another, as an eternal time.170) But how should Spinoza have allowed an infinite series of successive individual things, objectively and really springing from one another, to count as something existing in itself, and considered according to the truth?
The fault lies already in this series of individual and successive things, which Jacobi regards as something absolute, and it is Jacobi who carries the individual and time into Spinoza's infinity.

An idea, insofar as it is considered from its negative side against the imagination or reflection, is an idea because it can be transformed by the imagination or reflection into an absurdity; this process of transformation is the simplest.

The imagination or reflection is directed solely at individual things or at abstractions and the finite, and these count for it as absolute; but in the idea this individuality and finitude is annihilated by the fact that the opposite of reflection or of the imagination, the ideally or empirically opposed, is thought as one.

So much can reflection comprehend, that here things which it posits as particular are posited as identical, but not that they are thereby at the same time annihilated; for precisely in that it is only active, its products are absolute.
Thus, in that it posits both - the identity of that which for it only is insofar as it is separated, and the absolute persistence of the same in this identity - it has happily found an absurdity.

Thus Jacobi posits the abstraction of time and the abstraction of an individual thing, products of the imagination and of reflection, as being in themselves, and finds that, if the absolute at-once of the eternal substance is posited, the individual thing and time, which only are insofar as they had been taken away from it, are likewise posited along with it - but does not reflect that [they], in being given back to the eternal substance from which they are taken, cease to be what they are only when torn away from it; he therefore retains, in infinity and eternity itself, time and individuality and actuality.
zh: 这种经验性的无限，只是就单个事物被设定而言才被设定（《伦理学》第一部分，命题
第二十八）——而雅可比在上面他的演绎中却把单个事物绝对地设定为一个感受着的东西和一个被感受到的东西，但单个事物自在却绝对是虚无——雅可比毫不客气地把这种经验性的无限算在斯宾诺莎头上，可是没有一个哲学家比他更不会去假定这种东西；因为随着有限事物并非自在存在，这种经验性的无限和时间也就直接消失了。
雅可比说，斯宾诺莎断言：如果我们把一连串彼此相继、客观地并现实地由彼此产生的单个事物表象为一个永恒的时间，那只是取决于我们的想象力。170）但斯宾诺莎怎么会让一连串彼此相继、客观地并现实地由彼此产生的单个事物作为自在存在的东西、并且按真理来考察时也算数呢？
错误就在这串个别的、彼此相继的事物本身，而雅可比把它看作某种绝对的东西，正是雅可比把个别者和时间带进了斯宾诺莎的无限性之中。
一个观念，如果从它反对想象或反思的否定方面来考察，之所以是观念，就在于它能被想象或反思变成一种荒谬；这个转变过程是最简单的。
想象或反思只盯着单个事物或抽象物和有限者，而这些在它看来是绝对的；但在观念里，这种个别性和有限性却被消灭掉了，因为反思或想象的对立面、即观念的或经验的对立面被思考为一。
反思所能理解的至多是：这里那些它设定为特殊的东西被设定为同一的，但它不能理解它们因此同时也被消灭了；因为正因为它只是活动着的，它的产物就是绝对的。
所以，当它把两者都设定下来——既设定那个在它看来只有分离才存在的东西的同一性，又设定同一个东西在这种同一性中的绝对持存——它便幸运地发现了一种荒谬。
雅可比就这样把时间的抽象物和单个事物的抽象物、即想象和反思的产物设定为自在存在的，并且发现：如果设定永恒实体的绝对“同时”，那么单个事物和时间——它们只有从永恒实体那里被拿掉才存在——也一并被设定了；但他没有反思到：[它们]在被归还给那个它们由之被拿走的永恒实体时，就不再是它们仅仅被从它那里撕下来时所是的东西了；所以他在无限性和永恒性本身之中仍然保留了时间、个别性和现实性。

en: If the popular tendency of explaining is not satisfied with the fact that time is nothing in itself and that it is lost in eternity, and if Jacobi imputes to Spinoza that he wanted with his philosophy to bring about a natural explanation of the determinate being of finite and successive things, then it follows from the above what an explanation of time really is, namely an abstraction that is made in an eternal idea.

So Jacobi could make the abstraction of time immediately on totality, or on the proposition of ground, and in this way comprehend it out of the latter; but to find the abstraction as such and in this form in totality — this immediately sublates itself.

We obtain the abstraction of time if we isolate thinking from the attributes and do not comprehend it as an attribute of the absolute substance, as which it expresses this substance itself, but fix it, abstracted from the latter, as empty thinking, subjective infinity, and posit this abstraction in a relative relation to the singularity of being.

Through this abstraction, then, time is truly cognized out of eternity and, if one wishes, explained; but its deduction out of a community of singular things will give a more natural explanation, in that the presupposed, the singular things, are indeed already something natural.

Under the naturalness through which philosophy wanted to bring about its way of explaining, it is throughout evident that Jacobi understands nothing other than formal knowledge and reflected thinking and cognizing according to imagination; the passages cited above about Jacobi's concept of knowledge belong here.

In such a natural way, to be sure, no philosophical comprehending is possible, and in Spinoza there are probably few lines of this naturalness to be found; but since Jacobi understands by natural explaining the cognizing according to imagination, everything in Spinoza is surely supernatural, and thus Jacobi's assertion that the world cannot be explained naturally171) could find its confirmation most of all in Spinoza, who not only put it forward but carried it out.

But thereby all so-called naturalness falls away altogether, and with it even that supernaturalness, because the latter only is in so far as something natural is over against it, and it is neither a question of reason, as Jacobi says (Letters on Spinoza, S. 419), seeking to transform the extra-natural or supernatural into something natural, nor of its seeking to transform the natural into something supernatural172); rather, that naturalness, i.e. mechanism and causal connection and time, as well as the knowledge that proceeds along pure identity and analyses facts, is for reason not present at all.
zh: 如果说，时间自在什么也不是、并且在永恒中消失，这一点还不能让那种受人偏爱的解释倾向满意，而雅可比又强求斯宾诺莎，说他本想用自己的哲学去自然地解释有限的和相继的东西的定在，那么从上面所说的就可以得出，时间的解释究竟是什么，即一种在永恒的观念中作出的抽象。
所以，雅可比本来可以直接在总体性上、或在根据命题上作出时间的抽象，并这样从根据命题中把它理解；但要把这种抽象作为这样的东西、并以这种形式在总体性中找到，这一点却直接扬弃了自己。
我们得到时间的抽象，如果我们从诸属性中把思维孤立出来，不把它作为绝对实体的属性来理解——作为这样的属性，它表达的就是绝对实体本身——，而是把它从绝对实体上抽象出来，固定为空洞的思维、主观的无限性，并把这种抽象设定为与存在的个别性处于相对的关系之中。
通过这种抽象，时间就真正从永恒中被认识到，并且——如果人们愿意的话——得到解释；但从单个事物的共同体中对它作出的演绎，却会给出一种更自然的解释，因为被预设的东西，即那些单个事物，本来就已经是某种自然的东西。
在哲学想借以成就自己的解释方式的这种自然性之下，通篇可以看出，雅可比所理解的不是别的，只是形式的知识，以及依照想象进行的反思的思维和认识；上面引证的关于雅可比的知识概念的那些段落，就属于这里。
以这样一种自然的方式，当然不可能有哲学的理解，而在斯宾诺莎那里，恐怕也找不到几行这种自然性；但既然雅可比把自然的解释理解为依照想象的认识，那么在斯宾诺莎那里，一切就都是超自然的，于是雅可比那个主张——世界不能得到自然的解释171)——就最能在斯宾诺莎那里得到证实，因为斯宾诺莎不仅提出了它，而且把它实行了出来。

但这样一来，一切所谓的自然性就整个消失了，从而那种超自然性也一并消失，因为它只有在有一个自然的东西与它相对时才是；而且事情既不在于：理性像雅可比（《论斯宾诺莎的书信》，S. 419）所说的那样，试图把自然之外的东西或超自然的东西变成自然的东西，也不在于它试图把自然的东西变成超自然的东西172)；相反，那种自然性，即机械作用、因果联系和时间，以及沿着纯粹同一性前行并分析事实的知识，对理性来说根本不存在。

en: As for finally the mathematical parables of an actu infinite, which Spinoza opposed to the deception of the imagination and by which, according to Jacobi, he was supposed to have let himself be deceived through his imagination, Spinoza is so certain of his matter that he says: how wretchedly those who hold the actu infinite to be an absurdity have reasoned, about that the mathematicians may judge, who would not let themselves be detained by arguments of such a stamp in things clearly and distinctly cognized.173) Spinoza's example is the space enclosed between two circles which do not have a common centre, according to the figure which he also had placed as his true symbol before his Principles of Cartesian Philosophy, in that through this example he fetched empirical infinity back out of the endless driving-beyond of imagining and banished it before himself.

The mathematicians conclude that the inequalities possible in this space are infinite, not from the infinite multitude of the parts — for its magnitude is determinate and bounded, and I can posit larger and smaller spaces, hence larger and smaller infinities —, but because the nature of the matter surpasses every determinacy of number174); in this bounded space there is a real infinite, an actu infinite.

For in this example we see the infinite, which above was determined as the absolute affirmation or the absolute concept, at the same time set forth for intuition, hence in the particular, and the absolute concept is actu the identity of the opposed; if these parts are held apart and as such posited as identical, if this particular, posited as such as actual, is expressed in numbers, and if it is to be posited as identical in its incommensurability according to the concept, then empirical infinity springs up in the infinite series of the mathematicians.

Incommensurability, however, consists in this, that the particular is released from subsumption under the concept, is decomposed into parts, and these are absolutely determinate and absolutely unequal to one another, and that, when they — just now equated in the intuitive concept — are now compared with one another, they are no longer in identity but only in a relation.

In a word, this is nothing but the transformation of geometry into analysis, or more precisely — of the Pythagorean theorem, which alone is all true geometry, into the series of the functions of curved lines.
zh: 最后说到一个 actu 无限者的那些数学比喻——斯宾诺莎用它们来反对想象力的欺骗，而按雅可比的说法，他正是通过这些比喻，让自己的想象力把自己骗了——，斯宾诺莎对自己的事情是如此确信，以致他说：那些把 actu 无限者当作一种荒谬的人推理得多么可怜，这一点尽可以让数学家们去评判，他们不会被这种成色的论据在清楚分明地认识到的事情上耽搁下来。173) 斯宾诺莎的例子是两个没有共同圆心的圆所围住的空间，其图形他让人作为自己真正的象征放在他的《笛卡尔哲学原理》前面，因为他通过这个例子，把经验性的无限性从想象那无尽的向外驱赶中召回，并把它定在眼前。
数学家们推论说，这个空间中可能的那些不等是无限的，这不是出自部分的无限数量——因为它的量是确定而有界的，而且我可以设定更大和更小的空间，也就是更大和更小的无限性——，而是因为事情的本性超出了数的任何规定性174)；在这个有界的空间里有一个现实的无限者，一个 actu 无限者。
因为在这个例子里，我们看到那个在上面被规定为绝对肯定或绝对概念的无限者，同时也为直观、因而在特殊者中被陈述出来，而绝对概念 actu 就是对对立面的同一性；如果这些部分被彼此分开，并且作为这样的部分被设定为同一的，如果这个特殊者作为这样的东西被现实地设定、被用数字表达出来，而它又应当在其不可通约性中按概念被设定为同一的，那么经验性的无限性就在数学家的无限系列中产生出来。
但不可通约性在于：特殊者从被归摄到概念之下中解脱出来，被分解为部分，而这些部分是绝对确定的、并且彼此绝对不相等的；当它们——刚才还在直观的概念中被设定为相等——现在被彼此比较时，它们就不再处于同一性中，而只处于关系中。
一句话，这不过是几何学向分析的转化，或者更确切地说——毕达哥拉斯定理，唯有它才是全部真正的几何学——向曲线函数的系列的转化。

en: From this there results the true character of thinking, which is of infinity; for in that the absolute concept is infinity — in itself absolute affirmation, but turned against the opposed and the finite as their identity — it is absolute negation, and this negation posited as existent, as real, is the positing of opposites: + A - A = 0.
The nothing exists as + A - A and is according to its essence infinity, thinking, absolute concept, absolute pure affirmation.

This abstracted infinity of the absolute substance is that which Fichte — as I or pure self-consciousness, pure thinking, namely as the eternal doing or producing of the difference, which reflected thinking always knows only as product — has brought closer to our new, more subjective culture.

The [element] held apart from one another in appearance, the incommensurable, the difference as product, is in the last relation, in infinity, that is, wherein the opposed at the same time fall away, equal to itself, and the identity in relation to the incommensurables posited as being for themselves (in numbers) is an infinite [identity], a nothing; but the incommensurables not as these abstractions, being for themselves (in numbers), nor as parts subsisting without the whole, but according to what they are in themselves, namely posited only in the whole — thus the true concept, the true equality of the whole and the parts, and affirmative infinity, the actu infinite, is present for intuitive or geometrical cognition.

This idea of the infinite is one of the very most important in the Spinozist system, and in a presentation of the same it would have to play a greater figure than — as in the Jacobian propositions — merely ever to serve as an idle predicate to thinking, extension, etc.

In it lies precisely the most important thing, namely the cognition of the point of union of the attributes; but without this idea, Spinoza's highest ideas are presented in a formal, historical manner, as in the 14.
Theses [in Jacobi's Spinoza] the attributes and modes are added to the absolute substance in the common reflective form of properties.175)
zh: 由此就得出思维的真正性格，它属于无限性；因为绝对概念就是无限性——它自在地是绝对的肯定，却是作为对立面和有限者的同一性而转向它们的——，于是它就是绝对的否定，而这种否定被设定为存在着的、实在的，就是对对立面的设定：+ A - A = 0。
这个无作为 + A - A 而存在，并且按它的本质就是无限性、思维、绝对概念、绝对的纯粹肯定。
绝对实体的这种被抽象出来的无限性，就是费希特以我或纯粹自我意识、纯粹思维，也就是以差别的永恒行动或生产——反思的思维永远只把这种差别认作产物——，拉近给我们那更为主观的新文化的那个东西。

在现象中被彼此分开持有的东西、不可通约的东西、作为产物的差别，在最后那种关系里、在无限性里——也就是在那种对立面同时消失的关系里——是与自身相等的，而就那些被设定为自为存在（在数中）的不可通约者而言，同一性则是一种无限的同一性，是一个无；但是，不可通约者不是作为这些抽象、作为自为存在（在数中）的东西，也不是作为无须整体而成立的部分，而是按它们自在地所是的样子，即只被设定在整体之中，这样，真正的概念、整体与部分的真正相等，以及肯定的无限性、即 actu 无限的东西，就对直观的或几何学的认识而言是存在着的。
这种关于无限者的观念，是斯宾诺莎主义体系里最最重要的观念之一，而在对该体系的一种阐述里，它就必须扮演一个更大的角色，而不是——像在雅可比那些命题里那样——永远只充当一个加在思维、广延等等上面的闲置谓词。
在它里面恰恰有最重要的东西，也就是对各属性的结合点的认识；但没有这个观念，斯宾诺莎那些最高的观念就是以形式的、历史的方式被陈述出来的，就像在第 14
命题[在雅可比的斯宾诺莎里]中，属性和样式是以属性的那种通常的反思形式加到绝对实体上去的。175)

en: We briefly gather together the forms of infinity.
The true infinite is the absolute idea, identity of the universal and the particular, or identity of the infinite and the finite itself, namely of the infinite insofar as it is opposed to a finite.
And this infinite is pure thinking; posited as this abstraction, it is pure, absolutely formal identity, pure concept, Kantian reason, Fichtean I.
But set against this finite, it is for that very reason the absolute nothing of the same: + A - A = 0; it is the negative side of the absolute idea.
This nothing posited as reality, infinity itself not as subject or producing, as which it is pure identity as well as nothing, but as object or product, it is the + A - A, the positing of opposites.
But none of these forms of infinity is yet the infinity of imagination or the empirical one.
The first infinity is that of absolute reason; the infinity of pure identity or of negativity is that of formal or negative reason.

The infinite, however, in its reality as + A - A, of which the one is itself determined as infinite, the other as finite, or finitude in general, is that of reflection and of imagination, to which what was indicated above belongs, when a finite is to be posited as absolute, i.e. at the same time as another.

In Jacobi, infinity is found either as something idle or as the empirical infinity of imagination, and this misleads him into thinking that Spinoza, in his mathematical example (Jacobi speaks of several, but in the 29th Letter there is only one, and Ethics, P. I, Prop.

XV, Schol., it is not Spinoza who uses the example there, but he cites it from the opponents) wanted to present an empirical infinity as actu existing, and is satisfied by the mathematical example to this extent, that he finds in it indeed no objective and actual, but yet a subjective and ideal [infinity].
zh: 我们简短地把无限性的各种形式汇总一下。
真正的无限者就是绝对观念，是普遍者与特殊者的同一性，或者说，是无限者与有限者本身的同一性，确切地说，是那个就其与某个有限者相对立而言的无限者的同一性。
而这个无限者就是纯粹的思维；被设定为这种抽象，它就是纯粹的、绝对形式性的同一性，是纯粹的概念，是康德的理性，是费希特的我。
但一旦与这个有限者相对而立，它正因如此就是这个有限者的绝对的无：+ A - A = 0；它是绝对观念的否定的一面。
这个无被设定为实在性，而无限性本身不是作为主体或生产——作为主体或生产，它既是纯粹同一性，又是无——，而是作为客体或产物，那么它就是那个 + A - A，就是对对立面的设定。
但这些无限性的形式中，还没有一个是想象力的无限性或经验的无限性。
第一种无限性是绝对理性的无限性；纯粹同一性或否定性的无限性，则是形式的或否定的理性的无限性。
而无限者，在它作为 + A - A 的实在性中——其中一项本身被规定为无限者，另一项被规定为有限者——，或者说一般意义上的有限性，就是反思和想象力的那种无限性，上面所指出的东西就属于它，即当一个有限者应当被设定为绝对的、也就是同时被设定为另一个东西的时候。
在雅可比那里，无限性要么作为某种闲置的东西出现，要么作为想象力的经验性的无限性出现，这就诱使他以为，斯宾诺莎在他的数学例子里（雅可比谈到的是好几个例子，但在第 29 封信里只有一个，而《伦理学》P. I, Prop.
XV, Schol.，使用那里那个例子的并不是斯宾诺莎，而是他从反对者那里把它引来的）想把一种经验性的无限性说成 actu 存在着的，并且就这一点而言对那个数学例子感到满意：他在其中固然找不到客观的、现实的[无限性]，却毕竟找到了一种主观的、观念性的[无限性]。

en: Where we perceive a connection of ground and consequence (David Hume, S. 94), we become conscious of the manifold in a representation, and this happens in time, and this ideal succession is itself an actual one in the subject that produces it.176) — Spinoza has in this way accomplished more than he intended; for in his example he did not think of succession at all, and it is not to be seen in it either.

But Jacobi at least finds a subjective one in it; the example therefore has for him a psychological and empirical meaning instead of a philosophical one, only he does not yet find enough empirical material in it, namely, besides the psychological one, not also an objective actual succession, although the ideal one is itself an actual succession in the subject.
zh: 凡是我们知觉到根据与后果的一种联结（David Hume, S. 94）的地方，我们就在一个表象中意识到那杂多，而这发生在时间中，并且这种观念的相继本身就是它所产生的那个主体中的一种现实的相继。176) ——斯宾诺莎这样一来所成就的，比他心里所想的更多；因为他在自己的例子里根本没有想到相继，而相继在其中也是看不到的。
但雅可比毕竟在其中至少找到了一种主观的相继；所以这个例子在他那里具有的不是哲学的意义，而是心理学的和经验的意义，只是他在其中还找不到足够的经验的东西，就是说，除了心理学的那种相继之外，找不到一种客观的、现实的相继，尽管那种观念的相继本身也是主体中的一种现实的相继。

en: The nature of this polemical procedure thus consists in this, that Jacobi either misses succession and finitude and demands them in speculation unconditionally, or reads them into it and then finds absurdities.

The positive side of this being fixed in the finite according to the ideal form, namely in relation to knowledge, we have seen above, which is comprehended as proceeding along the thread of similarity and identity and as needing a fact that must be given to it as something foreign, the + B, to which the identity of the concept is represented as adding itself.

About this empirical knowledge in general, and about the individuality of sense, which determines the scope and the beauty of this empirical knowledge, and about the fact that through reason the empirical knowledge of the human being has a different character from the empirical knowledge of the animal, as also about the empirical presentation of subjective individuality or of sense, Jacobi sometimes has witty and ingenious expressions.
Such matters concerning the relation of empirical knowledge to knowledge, as (Reinhold's Beiträge, 3.
Heft, S. 92): that space and time are facts, because motion is a fact.
"A human being who had never moved could represent no space to himself; whoever had never changed would know no concept of time ...

a priori we would no more arrive at it than we arrived at pure manifoldness, at the connecting connection, at the productive spontaneity of the understanding"177), may perhaps belong to the compiler Köppen and not to Jacobi.
zh: 所以，这种论战做法的本性就在于：雅可比要么在思辨中找不到相继和有限性，就干脆要求它们，要么把它们解释进去，然后就发现种种荒谬。
这种依照观念的形式在有限者中被固定下来的做法的肯定方面，也就是就知识而言的方面，我们在上面已经看到了：这种知识被理解为沿着相似性和同一性的线索前行，并且需要一个事实，这个事实必须作为一种陌生的东西、即 + B 被给予它，而概念的同一性则被表象为添加给它。
关于这种经验一般，关于规定着这种经验的范围和美的感觉的个体性，关于通过理性，人的经验具有与动物的经验不同的性格，也关于主观个体性或感觉的经验性陈述，雅可比有时有一些机智而巧妙的说法。
这一类关于经验对知识的关系的事情，例如（赖因霍尔德的《文稿》，3.
Heft, S. 92）：空间和时间是事实，因为运动是一个事实。
“一个从未运动过的人，不能给自己表象出任何空间；一个从未变化过的人，也不会知道时间的任何概念……
a priori 我们恐怕同样达不到它，正如我们达不到纯粹的杂多、起联结作用的联结、知性的生产性自发性一样”177)，这些也许属于那位加工者克彭，而不属于雅可比。

en: The expressions of empiricism and about empiricism are full of spirit, because they allude to speculative ideas, and the interest of Jacobi's writings rests on this music of the sounding and resounding of speculative ideas, which, however, since the ideas break themselves in the medium of the absolute being of reflection, remains only a sounding and is not to grow into what, where the matter concerns science, is expected, into the articulated scientific word (logos).

If this sounding of ideas might be taken up into the concept as something objective, which it is not supposed to be, and be grasped and held fast as the common property of thinking, then, if one considers the sense of such expressions alone, one could not fail to recognize in them a presentation of reason.

For example, immediately after Jacobi (Letters on Spinoza, in the work cited above) had granted to reason only the capacity to analyse a fact and to connect it according to pure identity, he relates on p. 423 his basic thought: that he takes the human being without dividing him, and that he finds that his consciousness is composed of two original representations, the representation of the conditioned and of the unconditioned, which are inseparably connected.178) But is this then no division, which lets consciousness be composed of two representations that according to Jacobi are absolutely opposed?

According to the following page, we remain, as long as we conceive, in a chain of conditioned conditions and in conceivable nature; but this connection of conceiving and of nature ceases, and absolutely beyond, thus without connection, stands something supernatural, inconceivable and unconditioned.179) How then can Jacobi say that he does not divide the human being, since he lets his consciousness consist of absolutely opposed things?

Or rather, he already takes him divided, in that he considers him according to the appearance of consciousness. - But if we are really to take the human being and his consciousness and its composition as something undivided, as Jacobi wants to give it, then we must conceive that which Jacobi calls the principle of cognition and of reason as the undivided identity of the conditioned and the unconditioned, and, since according to Jacobi the natural is the former and the supernatural the latter, as the identity of the natural and the supernatural, and in this conditioned unconditionedness or unconditioned conditionedness we would have the same absurdity of the finite infinity that Jacobi finds in Spinoza, and at least the annihilation of the oppositions of the natural and the supernatural, of the finite and the infinite, thus at least the liberation from reflection, which makes the opposition absolute and the opposed things something in itself.
zh: 经验以及关于经验的说法很有灵气，因为它们暗示着思辨的观念，而雅可比这些著作的趣味就落在思辨观念这种鸣响与回响的音乐上；只不过，观念在反思的绝对存在这一介质里折断了自己，于是它始终只是一种鸣响，并不能长成——在事情涉及科学的地方所期待的东西——长成那清晰分节的科学之言（逻各斯）。
假如观念的这种鸣响可以当作某种客观的东西（它本不该是客观的）被接进概念，被当作思维的共同财产来把握并固定下来，那么，只要单看这类说法的含义，人们就不可能不承认其中有一种理性的展示。
例如，雅可比（《与斯宾诺莎通信》，见上文所引）刚把理性只判为分析一件事实并按纯粹同一性加以联结的能力，紧接着就在第 423 页讲出他的基本思想：他考察人时不把人分割开来，并且他发现，他的意识由两个原初的表象即受条件限制者的表象与不受条件限制者的表象组合而成，这两个表象不可分割地联结在一起。178) 可是，这难道不是一种分割吗？它让意识由两个按雅可比说来绝对对立的表象组合而成。
照下一页的说法，只要我们进行概念把握，我们就处在一串受条件限制的条件之中，处在可把握的自然之中；但概念把握与自然的这种联系中断了，绝对在彼岸、因而没有联系地立着一个超自然的东西、一个不可把握的东西和一个不受条件限制的东西。179) 那么，雅可比怎么能说他没有分割人，既然他让人的意识由绝对对立的东西构成？

或者说，他其实已经把人当作被分割的，因为他按意识的现象来考察人。——但如果我们真要把人及其意识以及意识的组合当作某种未分割的东西，像雅可比想给出的那样，那么我们就必须把雅可比称为认识原则和理性的那个东西，把握为受条件限制者与不受条件限制者的未分割的同一性，并且，既然按雅可比前者是自然的东西、后者是超自然的东西，就必须把它把握为自然的东西与超自然的东西的同一性；而在这个受条件限制的不受条件限制性或者不受条件限制的受条件限制性里，我们就会得到雅可比在斯宾诺莎那里发现的那种有限无限性的同一套荒谬，至少会得到自然的东西与超自然的东西、有限与无限这些对立面的消灭，也就是至少得到对反思的摆脱——这种反思把对立设为绝对的，并把对立面设成自在的东西。

en: Thus one could (Überfüssiges Taschenbuch, 1802, p. 30) very well understand the remark: where there is sense, there is beginning and end, there is separation and connection, there is one and another, and sense is the third180) , as a speculative idea; and (Reinhold's Beiträge, 3rd

issue, p. 70): "The mark of a sense in general is the two-endedness and the standing-in-the-middle between subject and object"181) , still more ibid. p. 95: "It is not sensibility that determines, nor is it the understanding; the principle of individuation lies outside them.
In this principle is given the secret of the manifold and the one in inseparable connection, being, reality, substance.

Our concepts about it are nothing but reciprocal concepts: unity presupposes totality, totality multiplicity, multiplicity unity; unity is therefore beginning and end of this eternal circle and is called - individuality, organism, subject-objectivity."182) But the middle of this circle, which is centre and periphery at the same time and holds fast the exchange, does not let the one disappear as the other emerges, would be the idea of reason, of the absolute and yet two-ended identity of the one and the many; such an idea, however, is a quite different knowing and cognizing than that which merely analyses given facts and proceeds along similarity.
zh: 所以人们（《多余袖珍册》，1802 年，第 30 页）完全可以把这句评语——有感觉的地方就有开端和终点，就有分离和联结，就有一者和他者，而感觉是那第三者180)——当作一个思辨的观念来理解；而（赖因霍尔德《文稿》，第 3 分册，第 70 页）：
“一般感觉的标志就是双端性和处于主体与客体之间的中间位置”181)，同书第 95 页说得更明白：“起规定的不是感性，也不是知性；个体化的原则在它们之外。
在这个原则里给出了杂多与一者不可分割地联结的秘密，给出了存在、实在性、实体。

我们关于它的概念全是交互概念：单一性以全体性为前提，全体性以杂多性为前提，杂多性又以单一性为前提；因此单一性是这永恒循环的开端和终点，并且叫作——个体性、有机体、客体—主体性。”182) 但这个循环的中间，那个同时是中心又是圆周、并且把交替保持住、不让一者消失而另一者出现的中间，将会是理性的观念，是一者与多者的绝对的、却又双端的同一性；然而这样一种观念是完全另一种知与认识，不同于那种只分析给定的事实、并沿着相似性前行的知与认识。

en: This shape, in which Jacobi raises reflection above itself only in a spirited way, is the necessary way out that results for the expression of reason when finitude and subjectivity are made into something absolute; as a spirited presentation, reason guards itself against taking up into [itself] the infinite of the concept and becoming common property and scientificity, but remains, affected by subjectivity, something peculiar and particular.

On the ring, the symbol of reason, which it offers, there hangs a piece of skin from the hand that hands it over, which one wants to do without when reason has to do with scientific relation and with concepts, - a spiritedness which, after the manner of the incongruity of a finite infinity, of something that is beginning and end at the same time, of a composition of the conditioned and the unconditioned, etc., again approaches more a formalism of reason, which is to be had very cheaply.
As subjective as the form of this philosophizing is, just as subjective and finite must its object also be; for finitude is something in itself.

The presenting and philosophizing proceeds at first to and beyond the human being: that we find ourselves placed on the earth, and as our actions there come to be, so too does our cognition come to be; as our moral constitution turns out, so too does our insight into all things that relate to it, etc. Against this perennial remembrance of the human being and the praising and narrating of his rational instinct and his sense, Epictetus speaks, forgetting the human being, in the passage that Jacobi (Überfüssiges Taschenbuch, p. 22) cites: But since I am a rational being, my business is (not to praise the human being [but]) to praise God; it is my calling, I will fulfil it.
zh: 雅可比只是以有灵气的方式让反思超越自身，他所取的这种形态，是当有限性和主观性被弄成某种绝对的东西时，理性的道说必然会走的那条出路；作为有灵气的展示，理性提防着在自己之中接纳概念的无限，提防着成为共同财产和科学性，而是受主观性感染，始终是一种特有的、特殊的东西。
理性递过来的那只戒指——理性的象征——上面还挂着一块递戒指那只手上的皮；当理性要建立科学的关系、要与概念打交道时，这块皮是人们想省掉的，——这是一种灵气，它照有限无限性、照某种同时是开端和终点的东西、照受条件限制者与不受条件限制者的组合等等的背理方式，又更接近一种理性的形式主义，而这种形式主义是极便宜就到手的。
这种哲学思考的形式有多主观，这种哲学思考的对象也就必然有多主观、多有限；因为有限性是自在的东西。

展示和哲学思考首先对着人并且超出人：我们发现自己是置身于大地之上的，我们在那里如何行动，我们的认识也就如何形成；我们的道德状况如何，我们对一切与之相关的事物的洞见也就如何，等等。与这种对人的永久记挂、对这种对人之理性本能和感觉的称赞与讲述相对，爱比克泰德在雅可比（《多余袖珍册》，第 22 页）所引的那段话里忘掉了人，说的是：但既然我是一个理性的存在者，我的事情就是（不是称赞人，而是）称赞神；这是我的使命，我要去完成它。

en: Of the peculiarity of not grasping the absolute in the form for rational cognition, but only in play with reflection concepts or in individual invocations, which, as Kant ends with the idea in practical faith, immediately also close philosophizing while they seem to begin it, or of being able to bear the rational only as beautiful feeling, instinct, individuality, Herder's philosophizing is only a slight modification; only that Herder's form even has the advantage of being something more objective.

The foam of Spinozism and the reason- and language-confusing preaching, as Jacobi183) calls Herder's philosophizing, springs precisely from this, that, as Jacobi puts the expression of feeling, subjectivity of instinct, etc. in the place of rational thinking, so Herder puts in the place of what is rationally thought something in which the rational is likewise veiled, namely a reflection concept.
The concept of power, like the concept of matter and of thought, says Herder (God, 2nd
edition,

[Gotha 1800], p. 126), developed (i.e. wrapped up), all three fall into one another, according to the Spinozistic system itself, i.e. into the concept of an original force; - the eternal original force, the force of all forces, is only one, etc. p. 169: The real concept, in which all forces are not only grounded, but which they also all together do not exhaust, this infinitely excellent thing is: actuality, reality, active determinate being; it is the main concept in Spinoza; - and nature (p. 245 ff.) is a realm of living forces and countless organizations, each of which in its kind is not only wise, good and beautiful, but a perfect thing, that is, an imprint of wisdom, goodness and beauty itself, etc. The withered hair, the discarded nail enters again into another region of the connection of the world, in which it again acts or suffers in no other way than according to its present natural position, etc.184)
zh: 不把绝对者把握为供理性认识的形式，而只在反思概念的游戏中、或在个别的呼求中拥有它——这些呼求像康德以实践信仰中的观念收尾那样，看似让哲学思考开始，却马上也叫它结束——或者只能把理性的东西当作美的感受、本能、个体性来忍受：赫尔德尔的哲学思考相对于这种特性只是一个小小的改动；只不过赫尔德尔的形式甚至还占一个便宜，就是它还是更客观一点的东西。
斯宾诺莎主义的泡沫，以及雅可比183)称之为赫尔德尔哲学思考的那种搅乱理性和语言的布道，恰恰由此而来：正如雅可比拿感受的说法、本能的主观性等等去顶替理性的思维，赫尔德尔也拿某种同样把理性的东西遮蔽起来的东西、即一个反思概念，去顶替被理性地思维到的东西。
力这个概念，正如物质和思维的概念，赫尔德尔说（《神》，第 2
版，

［哥达 1800］，第 126 页），展开（也就是卷起）之后，按斯宾诺莎体系本身，三者都落入彼此之中，也就是落入一个原始力的概念之中；——那永恒的原始力，一切力之力，只是一个，等等。第 169 页：那个实在的概念，一切力不仅奠基于其中、而且它们全体合起来也耗不尽它，这个无限卓越的东西就是：现实性、实在性、活动着的定在；这是斯宾诺莎那里的主要概念；——而自然（第 245 页以下）是一个活生生的力和无数有机组织的王国，其中每一个按自己的方式不仅是明智的、善的和美的，而且是一个完善的东西，也就是说，是明智、善和美本身的一个印迹，等等。枯萎的头发、被丢弃的指甲又进入世界联系的另一区域，在那里它同样只按它当下的自然位置起作用或承受作用，等等。184)

en: Does this not mean, as Jacobi185) says, to acquire the greatest merit of the researcher, to unveil and reveal determinate being?
Only not, as little as Jacobi, for philosophical cognition, but on the contrary with the effort common to both, to remove scientific form there where it is present for rational cognition.
Herder has a complete consciousness of the way in which he presents the centre of the Spinozistic system: "I would not know" (God, 2nd

edition, p. 77), "under which principal word the real and effective activities, the thought of the spiritual world and the movement of the corporeal world, could both be grasped so unconstrainedly as under the concept of force, power, organ.
With the word: organic forces one designates the inner and the outer, the spiritual and the corporeal at the same time.

It is, however, also only an expression; for we do not understand what force is, nor do we want the word body to be explained by it."186) Precisely this is Jacobi's business, to put expressions and words, which are not to be known or understood, in the place of philosophical ideas; they could well also have a philosophical sense, but Jacobi's polemic goes precisely against the philosophies in which seriousness is made of it and their philosophical meaning is expressed.
Köppen says best in the concluding declamation to Jacobi about criticism (Reinhold's Beiträge, 3rd

issue), what is at stake: Free, immortal being, human being, brother, full of high devotion, surrender, love, - how can the letter of your philosophizing reason teach you more strongly what you believe, hope and know more livingly in the innermost sanctuary of your soul: the rule of the infinite over you, virtue out of freedom and eternal life!187) etc. Such frosty and insipid outpouring of the heart, which comes from reason as instinct, to which Jacobi always refers, means, I suppose, to be more than a proposition of the philosophizing reason that wants to do without it.
zh: 这难道不就是像雅可比185)所说的那样，去赢得研究者最大的功绩——把定在揭示出来并公开出来吗？
只不过，他和雅可比一样都不是为哲学认识这样做，恰恰相反，两人同样努力的是：在理性认识本来有科学形式的地方，把这形式去掉。
赫尔德尔完全明白他是怎样展示斯宾诺莎体系的中心的：“我不知道”（《神》，第 2
版，第 77 页），“还有哪个主词，能把现实的和起作用的行动、精神世界的思想和物体世界的运动，两者都像在力、能力、器官这个概念之下那样自在地把握起来。
用有机的力这个词，人们同时指称内与外、精神的东西与物体性的东西。
不过这终究只是一个说法；因为我们并不理解力是什么，也不想借此把物体这个词解释清楚。”186) 这正是雅可比的事情：拿那些不必被知、也不必被理解的表达和词语去顶替哲学的观念；它们倒也可能有一种哲学的含义，但雅可比的论战恰恰针对那些认真对待这一点、并把它们的哲学含义说出来的哲学。
克彭在针对雅可比论批判主义的结语里（赖因霍尔德《文稿》，第 3
分册）把要害说得最好：自由而不朽的存在者、人、兄弟，满怀崇高的虔敬、献身、爱，——你那位作哲学思考的理性的字句，怎么能更有力地教给你，你在自己灵魂至圣之处更生动地相信、希望和知道的东西：无限者对你的主宰、出于自由的德性和永恒的生命！187) 等等。这种冷冰冰、淡而无味的心之倾泻，来自作为本能的理性——雅可比总是指向这种理性——它大概自以为比作哲学思考的理性的一句命题还要多，而后者正想省掉它。

en: A piece of polemic resting on the same ground as that against Spinoza: 'On the enterprise of criticism to bring reason to understanding and to give philosophy in general a new aim' (Reinhold's Beiträge, 3.
issue), this polemic against the Kantian philosophy we have here briefly to touch upon.

Jacobi's instinct against rational cognition has attached itself precisely to the point of the Kantian philosophy where it is speculative, and has made use of Kant's exposition, which is in itself not clear but is hindered by the terminology of a past culture — a terminology appropriated by reflecting thought and thereby become unusable for philosophical reason — and which loses itself on the speculative side into the product, in order with so much the less effort to galimatias it and to turn it into nonsense through and for unspeculative reflection.
The character of the philosophy of reflection expresses its principles in very determinate traits in this polemic.
zh: 一则与针对斯宾诺莎的那篇建立在同一根据之上的论战文字：《论批判主义要把理性弄成知性、并给哲学整个地指定一种新意图的事业》（赖因霍尔德《投稿集》，第3.
册），这则针对康德哲学的论战文字，我们在这里只须简短地触及。
雅可比那种反对理性认识的本能，恰恰粘附在康德哲学之所以是思辨的那个点上，并且利用了康德的那种表述——它本身并不清晰，反而受到一种过去教养的术语的妨碍，这种术语被反思着的思维据为己有、因而对哲学理性变得无用，而这种表述在思辨方面又消失在产品之中——为的是以更少的力气把它搅成胡话，并且通过非思辨的反思、为了非思辨的反思把它弄成荒谬。
反思哲学的性格在这场论战里以十分确定的特征把自己的原则说了出来。

en: A proper critique of this essay would also have to present the empty shouting and the biting, spiteful, and through distortions up to the malicious proceeding nature of it; to the latter we count such examples as occurs in the Vorbericht188), where on Kant's exposition of the forms of intuition an example is to be given of the disunity of the system with itself and of the mixing of empiricism and idealism, and to this end it is first documented in due form that space and time are mere forms, that they can never become objects, and for this the Critique of Pure Reason, [B] p. 347, is cited, where it says: 'The mere form of intuition without substance is in itself no object, ... pure space and pure time, which indeed are something as forms to be intuited, but are themselves no objects that are intuited', where not a word stands of their not being able to become objects (in which sense, we shall see presently).

'They can neither be intuited nor perceived', Jacobi continues, for which the Critique of Pure Reason, [B] p. 207, is cited, where nothing at all stands about their not being able to be intuited, and about perception it says that they are in themselves not perceived at all, because they are pure formal intuitions, not appearances (i.e. identities of intuition and sensation), not objects of perception.

And yet, Jacobi now says, these same forms of intuition, which are not objective, are according to other utterances also objects, for which the Critique of Pure Reason, [B] p. 160, is cited, where it says (in the note; in the text nothing stands about the object): space considered as object (underlined by Kant himself), as one really needs it in geometry, contains more than the mere form of intuition; — where Kant distinguishes formal intuition as the unity of the intuitive representation and the form of intuition, which in relation to the concept of the understanding appears as a mere manifold, but in itself has a unity, and, as § 24 also expressly remarks, that the understanding as transcendental synthesis of the imagination is itself the unity of space and time and first makes these themselves possible, [B 152-156] — one of the excellent points of what Kant says about sensibility and the a priori.

What contradiction then lies in this, that the form of intuition, as the pure abstracted form opposed to the concept of the understanding, is not an object, but can be made into an object as in geometry on account of its inner, a priori, yet in it as mere form of intuition not emerging unity. — Finally, a contradiction with the foregoing is supposed to lie in this, that space and time are not mere forms of intuition but intuitions themselves, and as such even single representations [B 136].

Single, individual (opposed to the concept) representations are for Kant synonymous with intuition, and this concept of Kant's cannot be called anything but excellent and one of his purest and deepest. — Even quite apart from the truth or falsity of the concept, where is there, between the above and what Jacobi adduces as contradictory, any other contradiction to be found than the one Jacobi brings into it by false citation?
zh: 对这篇论文的真正批判，还必须写出它那种空洞的叫喊，以及它那种尖刻、恶毒、靠歪曲一直弄到阴损的作风；后一种我们也算上一些例子，比如在《前言》188) 里就有这样一个例子：在康德关于直观形式的表述上，要给出一个例证，说明系统自身不一致、经验论与观念论相混杂，为此先按卷宗证明空间和时间是单纯的形式，它们永远不能成为对象，并为此引了《纯粹理性批判》[B] 第347页，那里说：“没有实体的单纯直观形式本身不是对象，……纯粹的空间和纯粹的时间，虽然作为形式来直观是某种东西，但本身不是被直观的对象”，——而那里一个字也没有说它们不能成为对象（在哪种意义上，我们马上就会看到）。
“它们既不能被直观，也不能被知觉”，雅可比接着说；为此引了《纯粹理性批判》[B] 第207页，而那里关于不能被直观这一点根本什么都没说，关于知觉则说它们自在地根本不被知觉，因为它们是纯粹的形式直观，不是现象（即直观和感觉的同一性），不是知觉的对象。

然而，雅可比现在说，这些同样的、并非客观的直观形式，按照另外一些说法又是对象；为此引了《纯粹理性批判》[B] 第160页，那里说（在注释里；正文中关于对象什么都没说）：空间被当作对象来考察（这在康德本人那里就加了着重号），正如几何学里现实地需要它那样，所包含的多于单纯的直观形式；——在那里康德把形式直观作为直观的表象与直观形式的统一体区分开来，后者在与知性概念的关系中显现为单纯的杂多，但在自身中却有一个统一体；并且正如第24节也明确指出的，知性作为想象力的先验的综合本身就是空间和时间的统一体，并且才使这些本身成为可能，[B 152-156]——这是康德关于感性和先验性所说的东西中那些出色的要点之一。
那么矛盾究竟在哪里呢：直观的形式作为与知性概念相对立的、纯粹被抽象出来的形式，不是对象，却又能像在几何学里那样、由于它那种内在的、先验的、但在它里面作为单纯直观形式并不显露出来的统一体而被弄成对象。——最后，据说与前面的话相矛盾的是：空间和时间不是单纯的直观形式，而是直观本身，并且作为这样的东西甚至是单个的表象 [B 136]。
单个的、个体的（与概念相对立的）表象，在康德那里与直观是同义的，而康德这个概念只能被称为出色的，是他最纯粹、最深刻的概念之一。——即便完全不顾这个概念是真理还是谬误，在前面那些话与雅可比当作矛盾举出来的东西之间，除了雅可比靠错误引用塞进去的那个矛盾，还能找到别的什么矛盾呢？

en: On the following page189) Jacobi says: 'Fichte, to whom it seemed incomprehensible how the I borrows its reality and substantiality from matter', etc. To this excellent presentation of the Kantian system, made thus in passing — as Fichte too is disposed of in an equally passing way — that according to it the I borrows its reality and substantiality from matter, the Critique of Pure Reason, [B] pp. 277 ff., is cited.

On p. 276 the period that runs over onto p. 277 reads: 'But here' (by Kant against idealism) 'it is proved that outer experience is properly immediate, that only by means of it, though not the consciousness of our own existence, yet the determination of the same in time, i.e. inner experience, is possible.'

To be sure, the representation I am, which expresses the consciousness that can accompany all thinking, is what immediately encloses the existence of a subject, but still no cognition of it, hence also not empirical cognition, i.e. experience; for to that there belongs, besides the thought of something existing, also intuition, and here inner ... , which itself is only possible mediately and only through outer intuition.
Remark 2.
With this all experiential use of our faculty of cognition in the determination of time also agrees perfectly.

Not only can we perceive all determination of time only through alteration in outer relations with reference to what persists in space (e.g. the motion of the sun), but we have nothing persistent at all that we could lay under the concept of a substance as intuition except matter alone, and even this persistence is not drawn from outer experience, but is presupposed a priori as necessary condition of all determination of time, hence also as determination of inner sense in regard to our own Dasein, through the existence of outer things.
The consciousness of myself in the representation I is no intuition at all, but a merely intellectual representation of the self-activity of a thinking subject.

Hence this I also has not the least predicate of intuition that, as persistent, could serve as correlate to the determination of time in inner sense: as, for instance, impenetrability belongs to matter as empirical intuition.'

We have copied out this passage in full, so that through the immediate view it may become clear how malicious the presentation, made so neat and bare, is, that the I borrows its reality and substantiality from matter.

For experience Kant requires something on which the change of time determines itself as on something persistent, and this persistent thing is matter, and indeed as something a priori, and substantiality is this persistence in time determined in relation to experience — from which predicaments relating to experience Kant expressly excludes the 'I am' and even the existence of the subject, so that what Kant says is toto coelo different from what stands thus in Jacobi without any explanation about reality, substantiality and matter, and gives to reality, substantiality and matter as well as to the I a wholly different meaning than when it is said thus in general: the I borrows its substantiality from matter.
Does it not mean, to cite and treat Kant in this way, to deal with him worse than with a dead dog?
zh: 在下一页189)，雅可比说：“费希特觉得不可理解的是，我怎么能从物质那里借来自己的实在性和实体性”，等等。对这种出色的、就这样顺便作出的——正如费希特也同样被顺便打发掉——关于康德体系的表述，即按照这个体系，我从物质那里借来自己的实在性和实体性，他引的是《纯粹理性批判》[B] 第277页及以下。
第276页上那句一直延伸到第277页的话是：“不过在这里”（康德用它来反对观念论）“所证明的是，外部经验其实是直接的，只有凭借它，虽然不是对我们自己存在的意识，但毕竟是对这存在在时间中的规定，即内部经验，才是可能的。”
诚然，“我在”这个表象所表达的是能够伴随一切思维的那种意识，它直接包含着一个主体的存在，但还不是对这个主体的认识，因而也不是经验性的认识，即不是经验；因为为此除了关于某种存在者的思想之外，还需要直观，而在这里是内部直观……，它本身只有通过中介、只有通过外部直观才可能。
注释2。
我们认识能力在规定时间时所作的一切经验性的运用，也与此完全一致。
不仅我们只能通过外部关系中的变化、联系到空间中持存的东西（例如太阳的运动）来知觉一切时间规定，而且我们根本没有什么持存的东西可以当作直观置于实体概念之下，除了物质；就连这种持存性也不是从外部经验里取得的，而是被先验地预设为一切时间规定的必然条件，因而也被预设为内感官在关系到我们自己定在时的规定，并且是通过外部事物的存在而被预设的。
在“我”这个表象中对我自己的意识根本不是直观，而只是对一个思维主体的自身活动的一种智性的表象。
因此这个“我”也根本不具有任何一点属于直观的谓词，可以作为一个持存的东西，充当内感官中时间规定的相关项：就像不可入性作为经验性的直观而属于物质那样。”
我们把这一段全文抄了下来，好让直接的观看表明：那个被弄得如此干净光秃的表述——说“我从物质那里借来自己的实在性和实体性”——是多么阴损。

为了经验，康德要求有某种东西，时间的变化作为在某种持存的东西上的变化而在它上面得到规定，而这种持存的东西就是物质，并且是先验的东西；实体性就是这种在时间中、在联系到经验时被规定的持存性——对于这些联系到经验的谓词，康德明确把“我在”、甚至把主体的存在排除在外，所以康德所说的东西，与雅可比那里这样不加任何说明地关于实在性、实体性和物质所写下的东西，是 toto coelo 不同的，并且赋予实在性、实体性和物质以及“我”一种完全不同的含义，不同于这样笼统地说：我从物质那里借来自己的实体性。
这样引用康德、这样对待康德，难道不就是说，对他比对待一条死狗还要更糟吗？

en: But the general spiteful treatment — that, when Kant rightly presents in experience the moment of sensation as well as of intuition and of the category as producing only appearance and giving no cognition of the in-itself and of the eternal, Jacobi conceives this 'as an eradication of all claims to cognition of the truth down to the ground, and as leaving over such a blind, wholly cognition-empty faith as has never yet been expected of human beings' — is comprehensible from his already indicated principle, that the finite and appearance are for him absolute.

Thus the Jacobian philosophy has also degraded the expressions truth and faith to the meaning of the commonest and empirical actuality, whereas of these words truth deserves to be used in philosophical commerce and faith has otherwise really and generally been used of the certainty of the eternal and not of the empirically actual.
Over the annihilation of such empirical truth and of faith in sensory cognition Jacobi rails, as over an assault on the holy, as over a church robbery.
zh: 但那种总体的恶毒处理——当康德有理由把经验中的感觉环节以及直观环节和范畴都表述为只产生现象、并不给出对自在之物和永恒之物的认识时，雅可比却把这理解为“把一切要求认识真理的主张连根铲除，并且只剩下一种盲目的、完全没有认识的信仰，而这样的信仰迄今还从未有人向人要求过”——从他已经显露出来的原则来看是可以理解的，这个原则就是：有限的东西和现象对他来说就是绝对的。
这样，雅可比哲学也把“真理”和“信仰”这两个说法贬低为最平庸的经验现实性的含义，而在这两个词中，真理是配得上在哲学交往中被使用的，信仰则本来也现实地普遍被用来指永恒之物、而非经验现实之物的确定性。
对于这种经验真理以及对于相信感性认识的那种信仰的毁灭，雅可比大肆辱骂，把它当作对神圣之物的侵犯，当作一次教堂劫掠。

en: To false citation and abuse there comes a third ingredient of the polemical presentation, namely galimatias-making.

The art of it is very simple; it is namely the grasping of the rational with reflection and the transformation of the same into something of the understanding, whereby it becomes in and for itself an absurdity, as we have seen that time has been galimatias'd into Spinoza's eternity and infinity.

Not to speak of such inversions — as when Kant calls the synthesis an action and then again says of it in relation to the imagination that it is an effect of the same, so that Jacobi takes from this the question: this faculty is an effect?190) — which the continuer also repeats faithfully and diligently on p. 85 and agrees with Kant that he calls it the mere effect of the blind imagination191) —, nor to adduce examples in detail, since the whole essay continues in a galimatias-making tone that takes pleasure in the preparation of nonsensicality, we set up the main thing, the relation of the so-called faculties as Jacobi conceives it.

It has been shown in the presentation of the Kantian philosophy how Kant, within this sphere, in an excellent way posits the a priori element of sensibility into the original identity of unity and manifoldness, and indeed in the potency of the sinking of unity into manifoldness, as transcendental imagination, but posits the understanding in this, that the a priori synthetic unity of sensibility is raised into universality and thus this identity enters into relative opposition with sensibility, and reason again as the higher potency of the previous relative opposition, but in such a way that this universality and infinity is fixed only as formal pure infinity and as such.

This genuinely rational construction, through which only the bad name 'faculty' remains, but in truth an identity of all is posited, Jacobi now transforms into a resting of the faculties upon one another.

'Reason ... rests with you on the understanding; the understanding on the imagination; the imagination on sensibility; sensibility then again on the imagination as a faculty of intuitions a priori; this imagination finally — on what?'
Obviously on nothing!
It is the true turtle, the absolute ground, the essential in all essences.

Out of itself purely it produces itself and, as the possibility itself of everything possible, not only of what is possible but also of what is — perhaps! — impossible.'192) Into such a fine connection Jacobi brings the faculties, and that something, though not the imagination as separated from the totality, rests upon itself, is for Jacobi not only as unphilosophical as the image of the stupid Indians, who let the world be carried by a being that rests upon itself, but also wicked; and because everyone knows from his youth and from psychology that the imagination is a faculty of fabricating, so according to Jacobi philosophy wants, through such an imagination, to persuade man that the whole man is really a web without beginning and end, out of sheer deceit and illusion, out of delusive visions, out of dream, that man has invented and fabricated for himself a religion and a language, etc., as is endlessly quarrelled and apostrophized about in the Taschenbuch.
