In short, Jacobi understands such an imagination as well as a self-generating reason as something arbitrary and subjective, and sensory experience as eternal truth.
zh: 在错误的引用和辱骂之外，论战性的表述还有第三种配料，那就是胡话化。
这种胡话化的技艺很简单；它就是借助反思去把握理性的东西，并把它转变成知性的东西，于是它自在地、自为地就成了一件荒唐事，正如我们已经看到，在斯宾诺莎的永恒和无限性之中，时间就是这样被搅成胡话的。

且不说这类颠倒——比如康德把综合称为一种行动，随后又在联系到想象力时说它是想象力的一种结果，于是雅可比从这里提出一个问题：这种能力是一种结果吗？190)——续写者也在第85页忠实地、勤勉地重复了这一点，并且赞同康德，说他把它称为盲目的想象力的单纯结果191)——；也不去逐一举例，因为整篇论文都以一种胡话化的、在制造荒谬中自得其乐的调子继续下去，所以我们把主要的事情摆出来：雅可比所理解的所谓诸能力之间的关系。
在表述康德哲学时已经指出，康德在这个领域之内以出色的方式把感性的先验之物设定为统一体和杂多的原初同一性，而且是设定在统一体沉入杂多的级次中，作为先验的想象力；知性则被设定在这一点上：感性的先验的综合统一体被提升到普遍性，于是这种同一性就与感性进入相对的对立；理性则又是先前的相对对立的更高级次，但这样一来，这种普遍性和无限性只被固定为形式上的、纯粹的无限性，并且作为这样的东西被固定下来。
这种真正理性的建构，其中只还剩下“能力”这个糟糕的名称，实际上设定的却是所有东西的同一性，雅可比现在却把它变成诸能力相互依靠。
“理性……在你们那里依靠知性；知性依靠想象力；想象力依靠感性；感性又依靠作为 a priori 直观之能力的想象力；这种想象力最终——依靠什么？”
显然什么也不依靠！
它就是那只真正的乌龟，绝对根据，一切本质中的本质东西。

它纯粹从自身中产生自身，并且作为一切可能之物的可能性本身，不但是可能之物的可能性，而且也是——也许！——不可能之物的可能性。”192) 雅可比就这样美妙地把诸能力联结起来，而说某种东西——当然不是脱离总体性的想象力——自身支撑自身，这在雅可比看来不仅像愚蠢的印度人那幅图像一样不合哲学，那些印度人让世界由一个自身支撑自身的存在者来承载，而且也是亵渎的；又因为每个人从自己的青年时代和心理学都知道，想象力是一种虚构的能力，所以按照雅可比的说法，哲学就想借这样一种想象力说服人，说整个的人现实地就是一个没有开端和终点的织物，全由欺骗和迷惑、由幻象、由梦构成，说人给自己发明、虚构了一种宗教和一种语言等等，正如人们在《袖珍手册》里为此无休无止地争吵和呼告那样。
总之，雅可比把这样一种想象力以及一种自身产生自身的理性理解为任意的、主观的东西，而把感性经验理解为永恒的真理。

en: On account of that galimatias-like presentation of the Kantian construction of the knowing spirit, Jacobi testifies on p. 52 that you see how well enough, incidentally, he has grasped your cause, and he will be so magnanimous as not to reproach you with knowingly deceiving.193) - The editor Reinhold annotates that truthful presentation with the remark that 'the functions described here the Kantian philosophy, insofar as it wants to keep even only the semblance of consequence, must acknowledge as the principles of its theory of the faculty of cognition silently presupposed by it; the Fichtean philosophy, on the other hand, sets the said functions up expressly, and indeed with an intuiting, thinking and willing of all of them'.
zh: 由于康德对认识着的精神的建构被那样语无伦次地描述出来，雅可比在第 52 页上作证说，你们看，他毕竟把你们的事情领会得够好了，并且他愿意宽宏大量，不指责你们明知故犯地骗人。193) —— 编者赖因霍尔德对这番真实的描述加了一句评注：“这里所描述的那些机能，康德哲学只要还想保住哪怕只是结果一致的外观，就必须把它们认作它的认识能力理论暗中预设的原则；而费希特哲学则明确地把上述机能建立起来，而且是带着对所有这些机能的直观、思维和意愿来建立的。”

en: The main question that Jacobi asks is: how does the Kantian philosophy come a priori to a judgement, how does it bring the absolute to the birth of finitude, pure time to times, pure space to spaces?

The eternal dilemma of reflection is this: if philosophy cognizes a transition out of the eternal into the temporal, then it is easy to show that it posits the temporal into the eternal itself and thus makes the eternal temporal; if it does not cognize this transition, it posits the absolute simultaneity of the totality for intuitive cognition, so that the different is not present in the form of parts and temporal essence, then it is defective, for it is also supposed to have and explain the temporal, the determinate and the singular. - The latter is the common thought of reflection, in which Jacobi believes he possesses a screw that the Kantian philosophy too could not resist.

He fortunately conceives, as cannot fail to be the case, the totality of intellectual intuition or a priori synthesis, which includes difference absolutely within itself, as an abstract unity, and thus has the parts not in the whole but beside the abstract unity to which he turns the whole, and necessarily finds that if a synthesis a priori were to be explained(!), then one would at the same time have had to explain a pure antithesis; but there is not the slightest presentiment of this need; the manifold for the synthesis is empirically presupposed by Kant and was nevertheless supposed to remain when one abstracted from everything empirical, as if the original synthesis were not an identity of the different.
zh: 雅可比提出的主要问题是：康德哲学如何先验地达到一个判断，它如何使绝对者生出有限性、使纯粹时间生出诸时间、使纯粹空间生出诸空间？

反思的永恒两难就是：如果哲学认识到一种从永恒者向时间者的过渡，那就很容易指出，它把时间者设定进永恒者本身之中，因而把永恒者变成时间性的；如果它不认识这种过渡，把总体性的绝对同时性设定为直观认识，以致有差别的东西不以部分和时间性本质的形式存在，那它就是有缺陷的，因为它也应当拥有并解释时间性的、被规定的和单个的东西。——后一种想法是普通的反思想法，雅可比自以为在这里握住了一个螺丝，连康德哲学也拧不过它。

他幸好把智性直观或先验综合的总体性——这种总体性把差别径直包含在自身之中——领会为一个抽象的统一体，因而他并不是把部分放在整体里，而是放在他使之成为整体的那个抽象统一体旁边，并且必然发现：如果要解释(!)一种先验综合，那就必须同时解释一种纯粹的反题；可是这种需要却连一丝预感都没有；综合所需的杂多被康德经验地预设下来，而且即使人们从一切经验的东西抽象出来，它也应当保留，就好像源初的综合不是有差别者的同一性似的。

en: But of course the different is not present in it as something purely finite, antithetic, as Jacobi wants to see it.
Original synthesizing would, according to Jacobi, be an original determining, but an original determining would be a creating out of nothing.

It has already been remarked above that for reflection the nothing begins where there is no absolute, isolated finitude abstracted from the absolute substance, and that the reality of reflection opposed to the nothing of reflection, the something of reflection, is absolutely nothing but this absolute opposition and absolute finitude.

That the synthesis is a pure unity, and hence that there is no difference in it, is the single and simple thought, stretched out into an endless clamour working its way into nonsense and into a quite unruly thumping and wrangling.

The idea of the synthesis, as of the whole Kantian philosophy, Jacobi draws from isolated passages, and if there Kant once, among other things, calls the synthesis the action of adding various representations to one another and of comprehending their manifoldness in one cognition, what is clearer than that he already presupposes the antithesis for his identity?

Jacobi duly muddles everything organic in the Kantian construction and makes time, space, the transcendental imagination arbitrarily clear and pure, all into pure solid unities that have nothing to do with one another; he makes himself into the absolute solidity of infinite space and then asks: how can you break into my solidity and let even a single distinct point arise in me? how can time, space, the unity of consciousness break into one another? - without considering that the purity of time, of space and of the transcendental imagination are fictions just as much as the fact that he is this quarrel-free and cloudless intuition of the infinite solidity of space.

With time Jacobi is somewhat better satisfied; namely he finds it as a bridge between the real and the ideal, the intellectual and the material, and can take it for a sense: it is two-ended and somewhere in a middle, and hence a sense, - which indeed is in general this two-endedness and standing-in-the-middle between object and subject.

But even if the imagination produces a time having beginning, middle and end within itself, it cannot say how large or small these produced eggs are; this it must determine by space, into which Jacobi passes over and posits himself as its infinite pure, untroubled identity and continuity, and, stuck fast in this unity, asserts that for all eternity a pure and empty imagination, if it were alone with space, could not produce a single point.

If a finitization is to be conceived in pure space, Jacobi relates very well, then that which posits this finitization (better: reality) must be something that is equally exalted above both, above pure intuition as above the pure concept, above the pure concept as above pure intuition, something that falls neither under a (sensuous) intuition nor under a concept.

This runs, for Jacobi, into the partly true, partly crooked determination: it does not itself intuit and itself conceives no concepts; it is an equal, all-purest doing of both and as such is called the synthetic unity of transcendental apperception.194)
zh: 不过当然，有差别的东西并不是像雅可比想看到的那样，作为纯粹有限的、反题式的东西存在于其中。
按雅可比的说法，源初的综合活动会是一种源初的规定活动，而源初的规定活动则是从无中创造。
上面已经提醒过：对反思来说，无是从没有绝对的、孤立的、从绝对实体抽象出来的有限性的地方开始的；而与反思的无相对立的反思的实在性，即反思的某物，恰恰只是这种绝对的对立和绝对的有限性。
综合是纯粹的统一，因而其中没有差别——这个唯一而简单的想法，被拉长成一片没完没了、越陷越深的胡言乱语，以及完全撒野般的捶打和吵闹。
综合的观念，乃至整个康德哲学的观念，雅可比都是从个别段落里汲取来的；而如果康德在那里顺便把综合称为把各种表象彼此加到一起、并在一种认识中把握它们的杂多的活动，那么还有什么比他早已为自己的同一性预设了反题更清楚的呢？

雅可比恰到好处地把康德建构中一切有机的东西搅成一团，随意把时间、空间、先验想象力弄得又清晰又纯粹，全都弄成纯粹的、结实的、彼此毫无干系的统一体；他把自己弄成无限空间的绝对结实性，然后问：你们怎么能闯进我的结实性里，让我这里哪怕产生出一个有区别的点？时间、空间、意识的统一怎么能互相闯入？——却没有想到，时间、空间和先验想象力的纯粹性，同他是一个无争吵、无云翳地直观着无限空间的结实性的东西一样，都是虚构。
对时间，雅可比多少满意一些；就是说，他发现时间是实在的东西与观念的东西、智性的东西与物质的东西之间的一座桥，可以把它当作一种感官：它是两头开口的，处在某个中间，因而是一种感官，——感官本来就是这样一种两头开口、处在客体与主体之间的东西。
可是，即便想象力产生出自身内含有开端、中间和结尾的时间，它也说不清这些产生出来的蛋有多大或多小；这它得靠空间来规定，而雅可比就转到空间里去，把自己设定为空间那无限纯粹的、不受搅扰的同一性和连续性，并且死守在这个统一体中断言：一种纯粹而空洞的想象力，如果只和空间待在一起，就永永远远也产生不出一个点。
如果要在纯粹空间里以概念把握一种有限化，雅可比讲得很好，那么这种设定有限化（更确切地说：实在性）的东西就必须同等地超乎两者之上，既超乎纯粹直观也超乎纯粹概念，既超乎纯粹概念也超乎纯粹直观，既不掉进一种（感性的）直观之下，也不掉进一个概念之下。
在雅可比那里，这归结为一种一半正确、一半歪斜的规定：它自己并不直观，自己也不以概念把握任何概念；它是两者同等的、最纯粹不过的活动，并作为这样的活动叫作先验统觉的综合统一。194)

en: With this word, that is, at the point where for the very first time perhaps the matter itself could have been spoken of, Jacobi's actual elaboration comes to an end; at the point where the hitherto thought-empty clamour and wrangling seemed able to gain an interest, because hitherto nothing but empty unities had been spoken of and only of a galimatias-ized understanding, imagination and reason, Jacobi breaks off, which he makes intelligible through the bulletin of his health in the preface, and at the same time wholly cancels any hope that he himself would still have followed with something better, by the fact that he (preface p. 5) no longer sees before him any of the actually dangerous passages, only a small, somewhat immovable, yet already more than half-cleared stretch.195) More intelligible, if it were not already intelligible enough from what precedes, this becomes especially through p. 61, where it is said that you try in vain to introduce a difference among your pure qualitative unities and continuities by giving one of them the name of a synthetic one (so the matter lies merely in the name). 'I say, the one can as little as the other divide and sum, the synthesis absolutely does not happen through it, for then it would also have to have in itself the ground of the antithesis: hoc Opus, hic labor; but empty space and empty time and consciousness impossibly have in themselves the origin of the antithesis.'196) - In short, the course of the matter is: the absolute synthetic unity, the totality, includes all parts and difference within itself; - but I, Jacobi, say: that is only a name, it is an abstract unity, an empty unity, how then can it be the ground itself of divisibility and antithesis?
zh: 随着这个词，也就是在这个也许头一回可以谈到事情本身的地方，雅可比真正的展开部分结束了；在这个此前那些没思想的胡言乱语和争吵看来本可以获得一点意思的地方——因为此前谈的只是些空洞的统一体，只是被搅得语无伦次的知性、想象力和理性——雅可比却中断了，他在前言里用一份关于自己健康状况的通报说明了这一点，同时也借此完全取消了人们可能抱的希望，即他本人还会拿出更好的东西来，因为他（前言第 5 页）眼前已经没有真正危险的段落，只剩下一小段有点挪不动、但已经开了一半以上的路。195) 如果前面的话还不已经够明白，那么第 61 页尤其使它更明白，那里说：你们在自己的那些纯粹质的统一体和连续性中间枉然想引入一种区别，办法是给其中一个加上综合的名称（所以事情只在于名称）。“我说，这一个和那一个一样都不能划分和加总，综合根本就不是通过它们发生的，因为那样一来它们就得自身中也含有反题的根据：hoc Opus, hic labor；但空洞的空间、空洞的时间和意识，绝不可能自身中含有反题的起源。”196) ——总之，事情的经过是这样的：绝对的综合性统一、总体性，把一切部分和差别都包含在自身之内；——可是我雅可比说：这只是一个名称，它是一种抽象的统一、空洞的统一，那它怎么可能是可分割性和反题的根据本身呢？

en: The concept of identity and of transcendental unity becomes wholly intelligible through the cordial friendship of the continuer.

In his case the passage on transcendental unity looks just as little dangerous and more than half cleared; he thinks that the monotonous thought running through 81 pages (not counting the preface), that the pure unity as Jacobi conceives space etc. is no manifold, perhaps still needs a few explanations.

In the stream that sinks from thumping and wrangling into dullness, the following is to be found about the a priori synthesis, at which Jacobi broke off: "Suppose there were a pure manifold, whereby then would the connection be possible?
Obviously through the fact that it would take place in a third thing!"
Köppen makes this clear thought clear in the following way: "Suppose we have a different in space, then its connection consists precisely in the fact that it is located in space."
Still clearer: "Suppose we have a different in consciousness, then the connection consists in the fact that it is present in consciousness."
More clarity: "What now connects the two spatial objects?
Space. What connects
the manifoldness of consciousness?
Consciousness.
The whole synthesis reveals to us nothing further than an identity."

What has gone before is made more intelligible by the following explanation: "Insofar as two objects are located in space, they are, as spatial, completely alike; insofar as they are located in consciousness, they are, as present in consciousness, completely the same.
What need is there here of a special action of connecting?
Is not the whole synthesis already complete through space and consciousness as passive receptivities? ...
The understanding thus does nothing but equate, and in order that this be possible, finding-equal and finding-unequal are presupposed ...
Every judgement is the expression of such a found identity ...
Whatever else besides the indistinguishable may be encountered in a judgement belongs to its material and therefore does not take its origin in the understanding.

And this business of the understanding, this noticing, this conceiving of an existing identity, for the sake of which the imagination must destroy everything particular, sublate everything different, should be called synthesis?
On the contrary, all synthesis is thereby sublated!"197)
zh: 靠了续写者的那份热心友谊，同一性和先验统一的概念就变得完全明白了。
在他那里，先验统一的那段文字看起来同样不危险，而且已经开了一半以上；他认为，贯穿八十一页（不算前言）的那个千篇一律的想法——即像雅可比理解空间等等那样理解的纯粹统一不是杂多——也许还需要一些说明。
在那条从捶打争吵一路沉入平淡乏味的河流里，关于雅可比中断处的先验综合，可以找到下面这段话：“设若有一种纯粹的杂多，那么联系靠什么才可能？
显然靠它在某个第三者中发生！”
克彭用下面的方式把这个清晰的想法讲清楚：“设若我们在空间里有一种有差异的东西，那么它的联系恰恰就在于它处在空间里。”
更清楚一点：“设若我们在意识里有一种有差异的东西，那么联系就在于它存在于意识里。”
还要更清楚：“那么是什么把这两个空间中的对象连接起来？
空间。什么连接
意识的杂多？
意识。
整个综合向我们揭示的无非是一种同一性。”
前面这些由于下面这段解释而变得更容易理解：“就两个对象处在空间里而言，它们作为空间性的东西是完全相同的；就它们处在意识里而言，它们作为存在于意识中的东西是完全同一的。
这里还需要什么特别的连接活动呢？
难道靠空间和意识作为被动的接受性，整个综合不已经就是完整的了吗？……
所以知性做的无非是等同化，而为了使这成为可能，就要预设找到相同和找到不同……
每一个判断都是这样一种被找到的同一性的表达……
在一个判断里，除开那不可区分的东西之外还可能碰到的其他一切，都属于判断的材料，因而并不起源于知性。
而知性的这番营生，这种对一种现成同一性的注意和以概念把握——为了它，想象力必须摧毁一切特殊的东西、扬弃一切有差异的东西——这就叫综合？
这样一来，一切综合反倒都被扬弃了！”197)

en: This, from Köppen, on the transcendental unity of transcendental apperception or of the productive imagination.

It is expressed very intelligibly, Jacobi's concept of knowledge, that we human beings receive things as facts through the sense and the supernatural revelation of seeing, perceiving and feeling, that what is thus taken from experience (which the better organized and better disposed human being makes better than the poorer organization and the poorer sense) is already and long since synthesized, does not first need to be synthesized by us, nor can it be synthesized; for our activity upon this synthetically given is the opposite of a synthesizing, it is an analyzing of it, and this analytic unity that we find in the object is so far from being a synthesizing, a connecting of the manifold, that rather the manifold, the material, falls into scraps through the analytic unity.

Space, consciousness etc., the objective world, nature, we can grasp only according to analytic unities and can only dissect; (Letters on Spinoza, p. 424) thereby an unoverlookable (i.e., end- and totality-less) field is opened up for our investigation, which we are compelled to work upon already for the sake of our physical preservation; those things whose mechanism we have discovered, we can, if the means themselves are in our hands, also produce.

What we can in this way construct at least in representation, that we grasp; and what we cannot construct, that we likewise do not grasp.198) The cognition of the understanding is an incessant equating, which we call connecting and which is only a continued diminishing and simplifying of the manifold, - if it were possible, down to its complete removal and annihilation.

(Pocketbook, p. 32)199) - We say on the contrary that transcendental imagination and rational cognition is something quite different from what Jacobi conceives, that it neither analyzes nature nor tears what is given apart into analytic unity and manifoldness, but, itself organic and living and totality, creates and constructs the idea of totality as absolute original identity of the universal and the particular, which identity Kant has called synthetic, not as if a manifold lay before it, but because it is itself differentiated within itself, two-ended, so that unity and manifoldness in it do not accede to one another, but separate themselves in it and are held together by force, as Plato says, from the middle.213) For sense Jacobi indeed admits a two-endedness, because in its case it can really seem that there is no question at all of its not having to do with a given object and, its own two-endedness notwithstanding, not being mere passivity and receptivity, - as if in its two-endedness and middle the ends were not themselves already there.
zh: 这是克彭关于先验统觉或生产性想象力的先验统一所说的话。

雅可比关于知识的概念把话说得很明白：我们人通过感官以及看、知觉和感受的超自然启示，把事物当作事实接受下来；这样从经验中取来的东西（组织得更好、心性更好的人比组织更差、感官更差的人把它做得更好）已经、而且早已是综合过的，不需要再由我们来综合，也不可能再被综合；因为我们对这个被综合地给予的东西的活动是综合的反面，是对它的分析，而我们在客体中找到的这种分析性统一，远不是一种综合、一种对杂多的联结，毋宁说，杂多、材料倒因这种分析性统一而碎成零片。
空间、意识等等，客观世界、自然，我们只能按分析性的统一来以概念把握，只能对它们加以解剖；（《论斯宾诺莎的书信》第 424 页）这样一来，我们的研究就被打开了一片望不到边的（也就是说，没有终点、没有总体性的）领域，我们仅仅为了自己肉体的保存，就已经不得不去耕作它；那些其机制已被我们揭示出来的东西，只要手段本身在我们手里，我们也能把它们产生出来。
我们以这种方式至少在表象中能够建构的东西，我们就以概念把握；我们不能建构的东西，我们也不以概念把握。198) 知性的认识是一种不停的等同化，我们称之为联结，而它只是对杂多的持续削减和简化，——如果可能的话，直到把杂多完全清除和消灭。

（《袖珍手册》第 32 页）199) ——我们则说，先验想象力和理性认识同雅可比所领会的东西完全不是一回事：它既不分析自然，也不把被给予的东西撕开成分析性的统一和杂多，而是自身既是有机的、活生生的，又是总体性，它创造并建构总体性的观念，把这观念当作普遍与特殊的绝对源初同一性；康德把这种同一性称为综合的，并不是因为有一个杂多躺在它面前，而是因为它自身在自身中有差别、是双端的，以致统一和杂多在它之中不是彼此凑到一起，而是在它之中分离出来，并且如柏拉图所说，被强力从中间拢住。213) 对于感官，雅可比倒承认有一种双端性，因为在感官这里，似乎根本谈不上它不是与一个被给予的客体打交道，而且尽管它自己有这种双端性，也不是纯粹的被动态和接受性，——就好像在它的双端性和中间里，那两端本身还不已经就在那里似的。

en: The thumping and wrangling of the essay in the Beiträge Jacobi has in the Superfluous Pocketbook of 1802 also prepared for the unphilosophical public and the palate of philosophical dilettantism, and to that end mixed sentimental Jean-Paulian additions into the bitterness, but disadvantageously appended his sentimental, biting edicts to sensible humorous conceits of Lichtenberg; for Lichtenberg's deep and good-natured whimsical humour immediately heightens, through the contrast, the impression of a shallow, bitter whimsical humour.

How far these decrying defamations of criticism, which serve no instruction, are well carried out for the effect of which alone something like this can be capable, namely to fill the unphilosophical people with gruesome horror and loathing of such a spectre as the Kantian philosophy is, through a sturdy Capuchinade, and how far such gnomes and sentimentalities as: The drive of every living being is the light of this being, its right and its power.
Only in this light can he walk, work only in this power. - No finite being has its life in itself and so also not from itself - the flame of its light, the violence of its heart ...
Manifold is the gift of life, manifold the awakening into it, manifold its guidance, its use.

Like the animal, the human being too awakens first as a sensuous creature on merely sensuous nature. - See there the smiling one, the babbling one200) etc. - to what extent all this is uncommon ingeniousness and edification belongs in another department of criticism.
zh: 《文稿》里那篇文章的捶打和争吵，雅可比在 1802 年的《多余袖珍册》里也为不讲哲学的大众和哲学票友的胃口加工了一遍，为此还给那份苦涩掺进了一些感伤的让·保罗式附加句，只是不利地把自己的那些感伤而尖刻的敕令接到了利希滕贝格那些有意义的幽默念头后面；因为利希滕贝格那种深沉而善意的诙谐性情，通过对比直接抬高了一种肤浅、苦涩的诙谐性情给人的印象。
这些毫无教益、只会把批判主义骂臭的诋毁之词，究竟在多大程度上有效地做到了那种唯有这类东西才可能做到的效果，即用一场结结实实的嘉布遣会式说教，让不讲哲学的大众对康德哲学这样一个幽灵充满可怕的惊骇和厌恶；又究竟在多大程度上做到了像下面这样的格言和感伤之词所说的：每一个活生生的存在的冲动，就是这个存在的光，它的权利和它的力量。
只有在这光里他才能行走，只有在这力量里才能起作用。——没有一个有限的存在把生命放在自身之中，因而也不是从自身拥有生命——它的光的火焰，它的心的强力……
生命的赠礼是杂多的，向生命中的觉醒是杂多的，对它的引导、对它的使用也是杂多的。
和动物一样，人也首先作为感性的造物在单纯感性的自然上醒来。——看哪，那个微笑的、那个咿呀学语的200) 等等。——这一切在多大程度上是了不起的机智和教益，属于批判的另一个门类。

en: As the philosophical essay in Reinhold's Beiträge, so the popular essay too contains passages that, to unprejudiced outward appearance, could have a philosophical meaning, e.g., p. 40, note (what is underlined is found underlined in the Pocketbook in this way): sensation, memory and imagination presuppose a first and original element of consciousness and of activity, a principle of life and of cognition, a being in itself, which as such can be neither property nor effect, can in no way and manner be something that has arisen in time, but is self-essence, self-cause (according to the Letters on Spinoza, p. 416201) but the causa sui has its origin in the forgetting of the essential difference between the proposition of ground and causality), must be something extra-temporal and in this quality is also in possession of an extra-temporal, merely inward consciousness.

This extra-temporal, merely inward consciousness, which distinguishes itself most clearly from the outward and temporal one, is the consciousness of the person, who indeed enters into time but by no means arises in time as a merely temporal being.

To the temporal being belongs the understanding, to the extra-temporal one reason. - One could think that Jacobi now holds the proposition of ground and the principium compositionis of the older metaphysics to be more satisfactory for reason, because he here himself excludes from reason as the extra-temporal what he missed in it, succession, - likewise that Kant's blind imagination is according to its principle at the same time contained in this reason, which is an indwelling and extra-temporal consciousness that clearly distinguishes itself from the temporal and outward consciousness; for what one calls seeing is solely in the outward and temporal consciousness.
Or if Jacobi continues: the understanding, isolated, is materialistic and unreasonable; it denies spirit and God.
Reason, isolated, is idealistic and unintelligent; it denies nature and makes itself into God.

The whole, unpiecemeal, actual and true human being is at the same time (which surely does not mean side by side, otherwise there would be two pieces and parts) reason and understanding, believes undivided and with one and the same confidence - in God, in nature and in its own spirit, - then we would [on the one hand] have to grasp the undivided faith as an identity of reason and understanding, i.e., as a simultaneity of denying God and making oneself into God, of the identity of the temporal and the extra-temporal, i.e., of an eternal time etc., without in the least galimatias-izing the Jacobian philosophy, as it did with Spinoza and Kant, in that it carries into the undivided what is characteristic of the isolated insofar as it is held isolated,202) - as, on the other hand, [we would have to grasp] this undivided faith as an undivided, a pure, pure, pure, waveless One, beginning-, middle- and endless one-foldness, without Derhood, Diehood, Thathood etc. (see essay in Reinhold's Beiträge, 3.
issue, passim).
zh: 正如赖因霍尔德《文稿》里的那篇哲学文章一样，这篇通俗文章也含有一些段落，从无偏见的表面看来可能具有哲学含义，例如第 40 页注（加着重号的地方在《袖珍手册》里就是这样加着重号的）：感觉、记忆和想象力预设了意识和活动的某种最初的和源初的东西，预设了生命和认识的一条原则、一个在自身中存在的东西，它作为这样的东西，既不能是属性也不能是作用，无论如何都不可能是某种在时间中产生出来的东西，而必须是自我本质、自我原因（按《论斯宾诺莎的书信》第 416 页201)，causa sui 的起源却在于遗忘了根据命题与因果性之间的本质区别），必须是一个超时间的东西，并且凭这一性质还拥有一种超时间的、纯粹内在的意识。
这种超时间的、纯粹内在的、与外在的和时间性的意识最清晰地区别开来的意识，就是人格的意识；人格虽然进入时间，但绝不是在时间中作为单纯时间性的本质产生出来的。

时间性的本质属于知性，超时间的本质属于理性。——人们可能以为，雅可比现在觉得根据命题和旧形而上学的 principium compositionis 对理性来说是更令人满意的，因为他把他在其中所缺的东西、即相继性，在这里自己就从作为超时间者的理性中排除掉了；——也可能以为，康德那种盲目的想象力按其原则同时也包含在这种理性之中，而这种理性是一种内住的、超时间的意识，它与时间性的、外在的意识清晰地区别开来；因为人们称之为看的那种东西，只在外在的和时间性的意识里。
或者，如果雅可比接着说：知性若被孤立起来，就是唯物论的、没有理性的；它否认精神和上帝。
理性若被孤立起来，就是观念论的、没有知性的；它否认自然，把自己弄成上帝。

完整的、没有被切成碎块的、现实的、真正的人，同时（这大概不是指并排，否则就成了两块和两部分）是理性和知性，不分地、以同一种确信去信仰——信仰上帝、自然和它自己的精神，——那么我们就必须［一方面］把这种不分的信仰领会为理性和知性的同一性，也就是领会为同时既否认上帝又把自己弄成上帝、既是时间性的又是超时间性的同一性，即一种永恒的时间等等，而丝毫不必把雅可比哲学弄得语无伦次，像它在斯宾诺莎和康德那里所做的那样，把孤立的东西在它被保持为孤立时所有的特征搬进那不分的东西里去；202) ——另一方面，也必须把这个不分的信仰领会为一个不分的、纯粹的、纯粹的、纯粹的、没有波浪的一，一个无始、无中、无末的单一性，没有 Derheit、Dieheit、Dasheit 等等（见赖因霍尔德《文稿》中的文章，第 3
分册，passim）。

en: Whoever had the desire and pleasure to let himself be chattered along a string of nonsensicalities and galimatias would find in these Jacobian essays the best opportunity in the undividedness of the extra-temporal and the temporal, of self-essence and of the empirical, etc. For these compositions are not to be understood as if the temporal were to perish in the extra-temporal, the empirical consciousness in rational intuition, all finitude were to sink into the infinite and only a totality were cognized as the in-itself, which is neither isolated understanding nor isolated reason, for then the terrible thing would follow that the finite being of things annihilated itself and the finite things became appearances and spectres; if reason cognizes the finite as not absolute, as not eternal, then the human being can (Pocketbook, p. 36)203) 'have determinate being only through fantasy, only annihilation through reason; and yet deprivation of reason is for the human being the worst, and then the opened human lot is a lot of the most horrible despair'; - no, according to this most glaring of all syncretisms reason, as the cognition of the extra-temporal and of self-essence, is also to leave the understanding, as the temporal and unessential, its right, and, if it builds a temple to the deity, to be so humane as to leave the devil his chapel beside it as well.
zh: 谁要有兴致和乐趣，让人用一根绳子牵着一串胡言乱语和语无伦次的话往前闲聊，那么他在雅可比这些文章里，恰好可以在超时间的东西与时间性的东西、自我本质性与经验的东西等等的不分状态中找到最好的机会。因为这类组合并不是要这样来理解：时间性的东西在超时间的东西里、经验的意识在理性直观里归于消失，一切有限性都沉没到无限者之中，只还被认识到一个总体性作为自在，而这个自在既不是被孤立的知性也不是被孤立的理性；因为那样一来就会出现可怕的事：事物的有限存在自我消灭，有限事物变成现象和幽灵；如果理性认识到有限的东西不是绝对的、不是永恒的，那么人（《袖珍手册》第 36 页）203) “就只有靠幻想才有定在，只有靠理性才有消灭；可对人来说，失去理性又是最糟糕的事，于是向人展开的命运就是一种最阴森可怖的绝望的命运”；——不，按照这种一切混合中最刺眼的混合，理性作为对超时间的东西和自我本质的认识，也应当让知性作为时间性的、非本质的东西保有自己的权利，并且在给神性建一座庙时也要人道一些，让魔鬼在旁边也有自己的小教堂。

en: From all the foregoing, both the positive and the polemical of the knowledge of the Jacobian philosophy, the character of this knowledge has emerged, namely that reason can analyze facts, separate the universal from the particular and go on in empty identity; and where a philosophy sets up an absolute identity of the universal and the particular, there this identity is again made absolutely into a universality torn out from the particular and the necessity is proved to it that to its universal a particular must first be added, or that it merely accedes to the given particular.

Where Jacobi himself acknowledges a two-endedness, a subject-objectivity, it must be in the form of a sense, a thing, something experienced, which may not lose its character of something given, of an unmoved opposition to the thinking subject, nor may it be expressed as a free idea of reason and common property of scientificity, but only as something subjectively ingenious, and thinking and being, the universal, which is formal identity, and the particular, which remains something given, the ingenious subjectivity and the objectivity of knowledge, do not come together in cognition; the given fact and the subjectivity thinking it, the one is like the other an absolute.
zh: 从上面所说的一切，无论雅可比哲学知识的肯定方面还是论战方面，已经得出了这种知识的性格：理性能够分析事实，把普遍的东西与特殊的东西分开，并且在空洞的同一性中一路走下去；而一旦一种哲学把普遍与特殊的绝对同一性提出来，这种同一性就干脆又被弄成一种从特殊中撕出来的普遍性，并且向它证明其必然性：必须首先有特殊的东西加到它的普遍上去，或者它只是凑到被给予的特殊上去。

在雅可比自己承认一种双端性、一种主体—客体性的地方，这种双端性必须以感官、以物、以被经验到的东西的形式出现，它不得失去自己被给予者的性格、不得失去与思维着的主体之间不可移动的对立，也不得被说成理性的自由观念和科学性的共同财富，而只能说成某种主观上机智的东西；而思维与存在、作为形式同一性的普遍的东西与始终是被给予之物的特殊的东西、机智的主体性与知识的客观性，在认识中并不走到一起；被给予的事实和思维着它的主体性，这一个和那一个是同样的绝对者。

en: We have now to consider the point of how the absolute identity that is not in cognition - and yet it must absolutely at the same time be for the subjectivity that posits itself absolutely - is for such a subjectivity; this relation, then, of an absolute finitude to the truly absolute is faith, in which subjectivity indeed acknowledges itself before the eternal as finitude and nothing, but even this acknowledgment it arranges in such a way that it saves and preserves itself as something that is in itself outside the absolute.

But to the universal separated from the particular not only the absolute identical of both is opposed, but also the particular, and Jacobi has extended faith also to the knowledge of the particular outside the concept, to the empirical immediate representation of common objectivity, in that he took this meaning from the proto- and foundational empiricists Hume and Locke, who are pre-eminently the ones who have sunk philosophizing into this finitude and subjectivity, put this grounding of cognition and criticizing of the human powers of mind in the place of cognition, posited the particular as such as the absolute, driven out metaphysics through analysis of sensuous experience, [and] whose reflection-essence, spun out more broadly and systematically on German ground and soil, is called German, i.e., Kantian, Jacobian and Fichtean philosophy.

Apart from the relation of faith to philosophy, Mendelssohn and others did not let themselves dream, when there was still a tradition of what is the object of philosophical cognition, that Jacobi extended the name of faith to the certainty of the common objective and thereby on his side gave to the certainty of common objectivity precisely the importance that Hume, Kant and Fichte gave it in another way, an importance that - since Jacobi by asserting it and Hume, Kant and Fichte by denying it, both parties alike make one and the same boundedness and finitude absolute - becomes quite the same for both, in that it is wholly indifferent whether finitude is something objective (in the common sense) or subjective, if it is absolute.

Mendelssohn in the case of the Jacobian faith did not think of certainty about temporal things, but of the certainty, not cognized through reason, of common consciousness about the eternal and extra-temporal; in that he (Letters on Spinoza, p. 92) expresses himself: "My religion knows no duty to remove such doubts otherwise than through grounds of reason, commands no faith in eternal truths."204) In that he speaks of eternal truths as the object of philosophy, he had the idea that philosophy does not occupy itself with the certainty of empirical actuality and that Jacobi too in his faith does not have in mind the Humean faith in sensuous perception.
zh: 我们现在要考察这一点：那不在认识中的绝对同一性——但它又必须绝对地同时为那把自己绝对地设定起来的主体性而存在——是如何为这样一种主体性而存在的；这种绝对的有限性对真正绝对者的关系，就是信仰；在信仰中，主体性虽然在永恒者面前把自己认作有限性和无，但它甚至把这种承认也安排成这样：它把自己作为某种自在地在绝对者之外存在的东西拯救和保存下来。

但是，与从特殊中分离出来的普遍相对立的，不仅是两者的绝对同一的东西，而且还有特殊的东西；雅可比还把信仰扩展到关于概念之外的特殊东西的知识，扩展到关于普通客观性的经验性直接表象，因为他从那些源初的和根本的经验论者休谟和洛克那里接过了这个含义——正是他们尤其把哲学思考沉进这种有限性和主体性，用对认识的确立和对人的心力的批判取代认识，把特殊的东西本身设定为绝对者，通过对感性经验的分析把形而上学赶走，而他们的反思本质在德意志的土地上被更铺张、更系统地编织出来，就叫作德意志哲学，即康德、雅可比和费希特的哲学。

撇开信仰与哲学的关系不谈，门德尔松等人根本想不到——当时还留存着一种关于什么是哲学认识对象的传统——雅可比竟把信仰这个名称扩展到普通客观东西的确定性上，并因此从他这一方给了普通客观性的确定性以休谟、康德和费希特从另一条路给它的同一种重要性；而这种重要性——由于雅可比通过肯定它、休谟、康德和费希特通过否定它，双方同样把同一种有限性和限制弄成绝对的——对双方来说就变得完全一样，因为有限性究竟是某种客观的东西（在通常意义上）还是主观的东西，只要它是绝对的，就完全无关紧要。

门德尔松在雅可比的信仰那里想到的不是关于时间性事物的确定性，而是普通意识关于永恒的东西和超时间的东西的那种不由理性认识到的确定性；他（《论斯宾诺莎的书信》第 92 页）说：“我的宗教不知道有任何义务要用理性根据之外的办法去消除这类怀疑，也不命令人信仰永恒真理。”204) 他既然把永恒真理说成哲学的对象，他心里就有这样的想法：哲学并不去管经验性现实性的确定性，而且雅可比在他的信仰那里所想的也不是休谟那种对感性知觉的信仰。

en: But Jacobi had in mind not eternal truths, but the truth of common actuality; this is what the first Jacobian declaration against Mendelssohn directly bears on (Letters on Spinoza, p. 215): 'Dear Mendelssohn, we are all born in faith and must remain in faith. - Through faith we know that we have a body and that outside us there are other bodies and other thinking beings.
A true, wonderful revelation!

For after all we feel only our body, constituted thus or otherwise, and in that we feel it constituted thus or otherwise, we become aware not only of its changes, but of something quite different from that, which is neither mere sensation nor thought, other actual things (underlined by Jacobi himself), and indeed with precisely the certainty with which we become aware of ourselves; for without Thou the I is impossible.
We thus receive all representations merely through constitutions that we assume, and there is no other way of real cognition; for reason, when it gives birth to objects, they are brain-phantoms.

Thus we have a revelation of nature that not only commands but compels each and every human being to believe and through faith to accept eternal truths.'205) - Here the knowledge of common actuality, sensuous perception, is not only included in faith, but faith and the eternal truths are restricted to it quite alone. - Jacobi continues: "A different faith the religion of the Christians teaches, - it does not command it, a faith that has as its object not eternal truths but the finite contingent nature of the human being." - So those eternal truths about having a body and other bodies and the determinate being outside us of other bodies and actual things would not concern the contingent, finite nature of the human being?

And what a poor nature that one would have to be altogether, which in relation to that first one is itself still finite and contingent, and what a religion the Christian one would be, which had as its object this still lower, still more finite and more contingent nature.
zh: 但雅可比心里想的不是永恒真理，而是普通现实性的真理；雅可比针对门德尔松的第一份声明直接讲的就是这个（《论斯宾诺莎的书信》第 215 页）：“亲爱的门德尔松，我们大家都是在信仰中出生的，也必须留在信仰中。——通过信仰我们知道，我们有一个身体，而且在我们之外还有别的身体和别的思维着的存在。
一种真正的、奇妙的启示！
因为我们毕竟只感觉到我们的身体是这样或那样构成的，而当我们感觉到它这样或那样构成时，我们不仅觉察到它的变化，还觉察到某种与它完全不同、既不是单纯感觉也不是思想的东西，即别的现实的事物（雅可比自己加了着重号），而且是以我们觉察到自己的同一种确定性觉察到的；因为没有你，我就不可能存在。
所以我们只是通过我们所假定的那些构成状态才获得一切表象，而且没有别的通向实在认识的道路；因为理性如果生出对象来，那些对象就是脑子里的幻影。

这样我们就有了一种自然的启示，它不只是命令，而是强迫所有每一个人去信仰，并通过信仰接受永恒真理。’205) ——在这里，关于普通现实性的知识、感性知觉，不仅被圈进信仰之中，而且信仰和永恒真理被完全限制在它上面。——雅可比接着说：“基督教的宗教教导的是另一种信仰，——它并不命令这种信仰，这种信仰的对象不是永恒真理，而是人的有限的、偶然的自然。”——那么，那些关于拥有一个身体和别的身体、关于在我们之外还有别的身体和现实事物的定在的永恒真理，就与人的偶然的、有限的自然无关了？
而那种相对于前一种自然本身还仍然是有限的、偶然的自然，又该是多么糟糕的一种自然；那种把这还要更低、还要更有限、更偶然的自然当作对象的宗教，又该是多么糟糕的一种宗教。

en: Since Jacobi in this declaration, which gains still more weight through the special circumstances of its occasion and the deliberateness thereby produced, expressly restricts faith and eternal truths to the temporal and the corporeal, it is wholly consistent to detest the Kantian and Fichtean philosophy, which is out to show that in the finite and temporal there is no truth, and which is great above all in negativity, in which it proves what is finite and appearance and nothing.

The Kantian and Fichtean philosophy, in holding fast to an immovable opposition between cognition and faith, immediately posits opposition, and thereby finitude as such itself, as absolute, but with the difference that this finitude is an empty one and nothing but the pure, infinite concept of finitude, whereby it becomes equal to infinity, while every content and fulfilment that this finitude gives itself and must give itself is supposed to be a nullity; Jacobi, however, demands this nullity in its whole length and breadth and raises an unruly hue and cry over the annihilation of this nullity.

Furthermore, no misunderstanding at all is possible about this, that the Kantian and Fichtean philosophy establishes the immediate certainty of the supersensible as faith, nor about this, that when Kant denies the ideas all reality on the side of theoretical reason, theoretical cognition for him is a determination through the categories, which have their reality solely in the sensible world and in experience, or which at any rate make possible only an understanding cognition, not a rational one.

If now Kant denies the concepts of reason all reality in the sense that they cannot be given in a sensible perception and in an experience mediated by concepts of the understanding, and that in the field of experience they are only regulative principles for the use of the understanding, then Jacobi sees in this, that a temporal and corporeal determinate being is denied of them, the annihilation of these ideas themselves, and asks (S. 36, Reinh[old's Beiträge] 3.

issue) every honest man, on his conscience, whether he, after he has once clearly seen that the idea is only problematic for corporeal and temporal knowing and experiencing and sensible perceiving, will now return to those, once and for all decided to be objective — mind you, in which sense — "groundless, or else for some cause", as to objectively true and real representations, and will be able to place an honest, heartfelt trust in them?

I say, it is impossible!"206) One must rather say: only after the annihilation of that kind of reality is it possible to gain a confidence in the ideas; whereas in the persistence of the dogmatism of absolute finitude and subjectivity, which places the eternal truths in bodies and other actual things, it is impossible.

As an example of the malicious distortions to which this blind hatred of the annihilation of temporality and the holy zeal for the good cause of actual things drives, a citation occurring on this occasion cannot be passed over (this is not to say that these, together with the citations adduced above, are the only ones of the kind, but they are only the only ones that we have looked up in Kant): S. 99 f., Reinhold 3.

issue, says Jacobi or Köppen: "It would therefore be far more consistent if, with all representations of God and immortality, we thought of no objectivity at all, and said with the author of the Critique of Reason: 'Everything that concerns religion and freedom is a mere idea of reason, a mere heuristic fiction, and, apart from its usefulness as a guiding principle of the understanding, a mere thought-thing of unprovable possibility.'

"207) — For this, the Critique of Pure Reason [B] S. 799 is cited; there it says: the concepts of reason are mere ideas and of course have no object in any experience; they are thought merely problematically, etc. Out of the concepts of reason, of which here there is talk solely in theoretical respect, Jacobi or Köppen makes, quite unconditionally and without restriction: everything that concerns religion and freedom, and this is supposed to be mere fiction — and what Kant says of their theoretical reality is pronounced of their reality in general.
zh: 既然雅可比在这篇声明里明确把信仰和永恒真理限制在时间性的和形体的东西上——这声明由于它起因的特殊情况、以及由此造成的刻意而分量更重——，那么憎恶康德和费希特的哲学就是完全一贯的：这种哲学所要说明的正是，在有限的和时间性的东西里没有真理；而且它特别擅长否定性，在否定性里它指明什么是有限的、是现象、是无。
康德和费希特的哲学固守认识与信仰之间一种不可动摇的对立，于是直接把对立、并因而把有限性本身设定为绝对的，但有一个区别：这种有限性是空的，不过是有限性的纯粹的、无限的概念，它由此变得与无限性相等；而有限性给予自己、也必须给予自己的任何内容和充实，都应当是虚无。雅可比呢，却要求这种虚无有它的全部长度和宽度，并为这种虚无之被消灭而发出狂野的号叫。
此外，对于康德和费希特的哲学把超感性东西的直接确定性立为信仰这一点，不可能有任何误解；对于下面这一点同样不可能有误解：当康德从理论理性方面否认观念的一切实在性时，在他看来理论认识就是通过范畴的规定，而范畴的实在性只在感性世界和经验里才有，或者说范畴根本只使一种知性的认识成为可能，而不是使理性的认识成为可能。
如果康德现在是在这样的意义上否认理性概念的一切实在性：它们不能在感性知觉中、也不能在由知性概念中介起来的经验中被给予，并且在经验的地域里只是供知性使用的一些调节性原则，那么雅可比在此看到的是——有人否认它们有一种时间性的和形体的定在——这些观念本身的消灭，并且问（S. 36，赖因霍尔德《文稿》第 3
分册）每一个诚实的人，凭他的良心：在他一旦清楚地看出，观念对于形体的、时间性的知识和经验以及感性知觉来说只是成问题的之后，他是否还会回到那些一劳永逸地被判定为客观的——注意，是在哪种意义上——“无根据的、或出于某种原因的”东西那里，把它们当作客观真实的和实在的表象，并且能够对它们怀有一种真诚的、发自内心的信任？
我说，这是不可能的！”206) 人们倒必须说：恰恰只有在那种实在性被消灭之后，才可能对观念产生一种信赖；反之，在绝对有限性和主体性的独断论还持续存在的时候——这种独断论把永恒真理放进形体和其他现实事物里——那就不可能。
至于这种对消灭时间性的盲目仇恨、以及对现实事物的善良事业的圣洁热忱会把人驱向何等恶毒的歪曲，有一处在此处出现的引文不能略过（这并不意味着这些引文连同上面举出的那些就是这一类里仅有的，它们只是我们在康德那里查过的仅有几条）：S. 99 f.，赖因霍尔德第 3
分册，雅可比或者说克彭说：“因此，我们如果在关于上帝和不死的一切表象上根本不去想任何客观性，并且同《理性批判》的作者一起说：‘一切涉及宗教和自由的东西都只是理性观念、只是启发性的虚构；而且撇开它作为知性的引导性原则的用处不谈，它只是一个可能性无法证明的思想物。’
”207) ——为此引了《纯粹理性批判》[B] S. 799；那里说：理性概念只是观念，当然在任何经验里都没有一个对象；它们只是被成问题地思维，等等。雅可比或者说克彭完全无条件地、毫无限制地把这里纯粹在理论方面谈到的理性概念弄成了：一切涉及宗教和自由的东西，而这是纯粹的虚构——康德关于它们的理论实在性所说的话，就被说成了关于它们一般的实在性的话。

en: Besides the fact that Jacobi has dragged faith down into actuality and sensible experience and speaks of this alone against Mendelssohn, he also has a faith not in finitude but in the eternal, and we must see whether this faith, which posits the eternal as absolute object and, separated from it and ununited with it, cognition, and thereby excludes rational cognition by the fact that cognition is acknowledged only as something subjective and formal knowledge, has not, through being placed in the relation to reflection, been contaminated even as faith.

The faith of the human being who does not raise himself to abstract reflection has the guilelessness that it is not opposed to reflection; it is without the reflection that the relation to the eternal in the form of faith, as an immediate certainty that has not been made objective through thinking and taken up into the form of the concept, stands over against rational cognition without necessarily contradicting it, and also without relation to an opposition at all — a pure, heedless position, not a negation, neither of another faith in something else nor of another form for the content of this faith.

To what extent the guilelessness of faith can be affected by that consideration does not belong here; the consideration alone belongs here: whether faith as such, when it is bound up with consciousness of itself and when it negates formal, finite knowledge — whether, with this consideration of finite knowledge, since no rational knowledge is supposed to come about, it is in truth capable of raising itself above subjectivity and finitude; it is in this negating, conscious shape that faith appears in Kant, Jacobi and Fichte.

The whole sphere of finitude, of being something oneself, of sensibility sinks in true faith before the thinking and beholding of the eternal, which here become one; all the midges of subjectivity burn up in this consuming fire, and even the consciousness of this devotion and annihilation is annihilated.

Also among the religious acts in which faith is feeling and beholding, there are more and less pure and objective ones, just as in song consciousness and subjectivity melt more into the general objective harmony than they sublate themselves in silent prayer.

But faith, introduced into philosophy, entirely loses that pure guilelessness; for now it is reason that flees to it out of reflection, in order to annihilate finitude and to sublate subjectivity; but precisely for that reason faith itself is affected by this existing opposition to reflection and subjectivity.

There remains in it — for here it has at the same time the meaning of this negating — the reflection on the annihilation of reflection and the subjectivity of the consciousness of the annihilation of subjectivity, and subjectivity has thus saved itself in its very annihilation.
Because in the consciousness that does not reflect on its faith, finite thinking and faith lie apart, such a consciousness is, on account of this lying apart, an unphilosophical consciousness.

Finite doing and bustling and sensible perception — and on the other side divine service — alternate with one another, and if for the religious human being everything finite and objective at the same time presents itself under a shape of eternity and his doing likewise expresses such a shape, then this shape of eternity is here something subjective, it is the ethical individual beauty that presents itself.

This beauty receives true objectivity and universality in art and philosophy, in which the opposition of faith and reflection, relating to the absolute, disappears, both insofar as it is present unconsciously in ordinary consciousness and insofar as it is present consciously in philosophies of reflection.

Insofar as it is present unconsciously in ordinary consciousness, faith and what comes from faith can be pure, for subjectivity and finitude lie wholly beyond, without contact with or relation to it; but the faith introduced into philosophy does not remain so, for here it has a consideration and meaning of negating, and in this negating it touches and thereby receives subjectivity.

It is affected by the opposition itself, just as that which constitutes its content, as supersensible, has an immovable sensibility over against it, the infinite an immovable finitude; and because in it both are present, annihilated and saved subjectivity, this subjectivity is justified, for it appeals to its being annihilated, whereas in ordinary, heedless faith it has on the contrary truly disappeared and is something unholy before it.
zh: 除了雅可比把信仰拖进了现实性和感性经验、并且只就这种信仰来反对门德尔松之外，他还有一种不是对有限性、而是对永恒者的信仰；我们必须看看，这种信仰——它把永恒者设定为绝对客体，而把认识设定为与它分离的、未与之结合的东西，并且由于认识只被承认为某种主观的、形式的知识，就把理性的认识排除掉了——是否由于被置入与反思的关系之中，就连作为信仰也已经被污染了。
没有上升到抽象反思的人，其信仰有一种无邪：它并不与反思相对立；它既没有那种反思——对永恒者的关系采取信仰的形式，作为一种直接确定性，这种确定性没有通过思维被弄得客观、也没有被纳入概念的形式，于是它站在理性认识对面，却不必与理性认识相冲突——也根本没有任何对立的关系——它是一种纯粹的、无所顾忌的肯定，而不是否定，既不是对另一种信仰、对别的东西的否定，也不是对这种信仰内容的另一种形式的否定。
信仰的无邪能否被那种顾虑所影响，不属于这里；这里只涉及那种顾虑：当信仰作为信仰与关于自身的意识结合在一起，并且否定形式的、有限的知识时，它带着这种对有限知识的顾虑——既然不应有任何合理的知识产生出来——是否真的能够超出主体性和有限性；正是在这种否定的、有意识的形态里，信仰出现在康德、雅可比和费希特那里。
有限性、自己作为某种东西存在、感性的整个领域，都在真正的信仰里沉没于对永恒者的思维和观照之前，二者在这里合而为一；主体性的所有蚊蚋都在这吞噬一切的火焰里烧尽，甚至连这种献身和消灭的意识也被消灭了。
在信仰是情感和观照的那些宗教行为中，也有比较纯粹、比较客观的与不那么纯粹、不那么客观的，正如在歌唱中意识和主体性更多地融入普遍客观的和谐，而在默祷中则是扬弃自身。
但信仰一旦被引入哲学，就完全失去了那种纯粹的无邪；因为这时是理性从反思中逃向它，为的是消灭有限性、扬弃主体性；但正因如此，信仰本身就受到这种现成的、对反思和主体性的对立的影响。
在它之中留存下来的是——因为它在这里同时具有这种否定的含义——对反思之被消灭的反思，以及主体性之被消灭这一意识的主体性；主体性就这样在自己的消灭中把自己救了下来。
由于在不反思自己信仰的意识里，有限的思维和信仰是分开的，所以由于这种分开，这样一种意识就是非哲学的意识。
有限的活动和忙碌以及感性知觉——在另一侧则是礼拜——彼此交替；如果对宗教的人来说，一切有限的、客观的东西同时以永恒的一种形态呈现在他面前，他的活动也表达出这样一种形态，那么这种永恒的形态在此就是某种主观的东西，它就是呈现出来的伦理的个别之美。
这种美在艺术和哲学里获得真正的客观性和普遍性，在这两者中，信仰与反思之间那种关涉到绝对者的对立消失了，无论这对立是无意识地存在于普通意识里，还是有意识地存在于反思哲学里。
由于这对立无意识地存在于普通意识里，信仰以及从信仰而来的东西就能够是纯粹的，因为主体性和有限性完全在彼岸，与它没有接触、也没有关系；但被引入哲学的信仰却不复如此，因为在这里它有一种顾虑、一种否定的含义，而在这种否定中它有所触及，并因此获得了主体性。
它受到对立本身的感染，正如构成它内容的东西作为超感性的东西，有一个不可动摇的感性东西与它相对，无限者有一个不可动摇的有限者与它相对；而因为在他之中两者俱在，即被消灭的主体性和被拯救的主体性，所以这种主体性是有理的，因为它诉诸自己的被消灭；相反，在普通的、无所顾忌的信仰里，它倒是真正消失了，在那种信仰面前是某种不神圣的东西。

en: This contamination of faith and this sanctification of subjectivity must still briefly lead us to Jacobi's practical philosophy.

Kant's practical reason, or the empty concept in its immovable opposition to nature, can produce nothing other than a system of tyranny and of the tearing apart of ethical life and beauty, or, like the Kantian morality, can hold to determining-nothing, formal, so-called duties, whose enumeration and presentation, in scientific inconsistency, gives way to the consistency of nature; and this side alone, in that in the possibility of a casuistry it at the same time confesses scientific nullity, makes the striving of ethical ideas visible.

But in the doctrine of right, determination must take place; here it will not do to let determinacy pass over again into the indeterminate, and this science has therefore necessarily had to besmirch ethical nature with the most glaring infamies.

The general hatred of Jacobi's philosophy for the concept necessarily disdains its objective form of ethical life, law, and quite especially the pure law as formal principle of morals, and among other excellent passages on this, the one in the Letter to Fichte, S. 32, is beautiful and wholly pure: "Yes, I am the atheist and godless one who, contrary to the will that wills nothing — will lie, as Desdemona lied in dying; will lie and deceive like Pylades presenting himself for Orestes, will murder like Timoleon; will break law and oath like Epaminondas, like Johann de Witt; will resolve on suicide like Otho; will commit temple robbery like David — yes, will pluck ears of corn on the Sabbath, and only because I am hungry and the law was made for the sake of man, not man for the sake of the law ...

For with the holiest certainty that I have in me, I know that the privilegium aggratiandi on account of such crimes against the pure letter of the absolutely universal law of reason is the proper right of majesty of the human being, the seal of his dignity, of his divine nature.208)
zh: 信仰的这种受污染和主体性的这种被神圣化，还必定会让我们简短地转到雅可比的实践哲学上去。
康德的实践理性，或者说处于与自然的不可动摇的对立之中的空洞概念，所能产生出来的无非是一个专制、以及把伦理和美撕裂开来的体系；或者像康德的道德那样，固守于那些不规定任何东西的、形式的、所谓义务，而对它们的列举和陈述，在科学上的一贯性上却让位于自然的一贯性；而唯独这一方面，由于它在一种决疑术的可能性里同时承认了科学上的虚无，使伦理观念的努力显得可见。
但在权利学说里必须作出规定；在这里，让规定性重新转入无规定的东西是不行的，所以这门科学必然不得不以最刺眼的无耻行径去玷污伦理的自然。

雅可比哲学对概念的普遍仇恨，必然鄙视概念的客观的伦理形式，即法律，更不用说作为形式道德原则的纯粹法律；在这方面，除了其他出色的段落之外，《致费希特的信》S. 32 上那一段又美又纯粹：“是的，我就是那个无神论者和不信神的人，他违背那个什么都不意愿的意志——要撒谎，像苔丝狄蒙娜临死时那样撒谎；要撒谎和欺骗，像为俄瑞斯忒斯而现身的皮拉德斯；要杀人，像提摩勒翁；要破坏法律和誓言，像埃帕米农达斯、像约翰·德·维特；要决意自杀，像奥托；要抢劫神庙，像大卫——是的，还要在安息日掐麦穗，也只是因为我饿了，而法律是为人的缘故制定的，不是人为法律的缘故……
因为凭我心中最神圣的确定性，我知道：由于这类违背绝对普遍的理性法则的纯粹字面的罪行而享有的 privilegium aggratiandi，正是人真正的君王特权，是他尊严、他神圣本性的印记。208)

en: We have called this passage in Jacobi quite pure, in so far as — for speaking in the first person, I am and I will, cannot harm its objectivity — the expression that the law is made for the sake of man and not man for the sake of the law, without regard to the meaning that this expression has where it is taken from, gains in this context indeed a more general meaning, but keeps its true one. - Neither side may be missing from ethical beauty: neither its liveliness as individuality, so that it does not obey the dead concept, nor the form of the concept and of the law, universality and objectivity, the side that Kant alone posited through absolute abstraction and to which he utterly subjected liveliness and thereby killed it.

The passage cited, which concerns the side of the liveliness and freedom of ethical life, does not exclude its objectivity, but neither does it express it, and as for its necessity and objectivity we must look around for other data.
Even what is picked out in the way of examples of ethical characters, by which Jacobi wants to make his idea of ethical life clear, shows the neglect of the lawful and objective side.

With the Spartans Sperthias and Bulis (Briefe über Spinoza, S. 240) it is their experience that determines their ethical conduct; they do not say, Jacobi notes, to Hydarnes, who wanted to persuade them to become friends of the king: you are a fool; they rather admitted that he was wise in his measure, discerning and good.
Nor did they attempt to bring their truth home to him.
They did not appeal to their understanding, to their fine judgement, but only to things and to their inclination towards these things.

They also boasted of no virtue and had no philosophy either; they confessed only the sense of their heart, their affect, and before Xerxes they became no more explicit than before Hydarnes, to whom they named their experience.

For to Xerxes they said: "How could we live here, abandon our land, our laws and such men, that we have voluntarily undertaken so long a journey in order to die for them?"209) But can there be a greater explicitness of the ethical?
Is only subjectivity of experience, of sense, of an inclination visible here?

To the satrap they proved precisely their contempt, in that they spoke to him of his and their experience and inclination and opposed their essence to his subjectivity in the form of a subjectivity; but to the majesty of the monarch they proved their reverence, in that they became wholly explicit before him and named what is most objective and as holy for him as for them, namely land, people and laws.

But Jacobi calls what is the most living, fatherland, people and laws, things to which they are accustomed, as one is accustomed to things; he does not conceive them as holy things but as common ones, for towards holy things there is no relation of being accustomed and of dependence.

He conceives as a contingency and dependence — in which lies the highest necessity and the highest energy of ethical freedom — living in accordance with the laws of a people, and of the Spartan people at that, - as something commonly empirical, what is the most rational.

The wretchedness of subjectivity, however, appealing to fine judgement and understanding or boasting of a virtue, was in any case not to be expected of them, and the absence of such wretchedness is something too poor to be singled out in them as a virtue. - Still less is there any thought of highlighting objectivity in Cleomenes in [Jacobi's] Woldemar, since this Spartan is introduced here not in his relations with his fatherland and in the strength of his true virtue, but in the individuality of his downfall; and to edify whom? - affected or insignificant women and sentimental citizens.
zh: 我们把雅可比这一段称为完全纯粹的，因为——用第一人称说话，“我是”和“我要”，并不会损害它的客观性——“法律是为人的缘故、而不是人为法律的缘故而设的”这个说法，撇开它在被取来的地方所具有的含义，在这个上下文里固然获得了一种更一般的含义，却仍然保有自己的真实含义。——伦理的美哪一边都不能缺：既不能缺它作为个体性的生动性，即它不听从死的概念，也不能缺概念和法律的形式，即普遍性和客观性；这一面是康德仅仅通过绝对抽象设定起来的，他使生动性完全服从于它，并且把它杀死了。
所引的这一段讲的是伦理的生动性和自由这一面，它并不排除伦理的客观性，但也没有把客观性表达出来；至于伦理的必然性和客观性，我们还得另找别的材料来看。
单是那些被挑出来当作伦理性格例子的东西——雅可比想借它们讲清自己的伦理观念——就已经显示出对法律的和客观的这一面的忽视。
在斯巴达人斯佩尔提阿斯和布利斯那里（《论斯宾诺莎的书信》，S. 240），决定他们伦理的是他们的经验；雅可比指出，对那个想劝他们做国王之友的叙达尔涅斯，他们没有说：你是个蠢人；他们反倒承认，就他自己的尺度而言他是明智的、有见识的、善良的。
他们也没有试图让他接受他们的真理。
他们并不援引自己的知性、自己精细的判断，而只援引事情本身，以及自己对这些事情的爱好。
他们也不夸耀任何德性，也没有什么哲学；他们只坦白自己心意的意思、自己的激情，而在薛西斯面前他们并不比在叙达尔涅斯面前说得更明白——对后者，他们只是说出了自己的经验。
因为他们对薛西斯说：“我们怎么还能在这里生活，放弃我们的国家、我们的法律和这样一些人——为了他们去死，我们才自愿走了这么远的路？”209) 可是，伦理的东西还能有比这更明白的表达吗？
这里看得见的，仅仅是有经验、心意、爱好的主观性吗？
他们对这位总督恰恰表明了自己的蔑视：他们对他谈他和他们的经验与爱好，以主观性的形式把自己的本质与他的主观性对立起来；而面对君主的尊严，他们表明了自己的敬畏：在他面前他们说得完全明白，并且说出了最客观、对他和对他们同样神圣的东西，即土地、人民和法律。
但雅可比把最生动的东西——祖国、人民和法律——叫作他们已习惯的事情，就像人习惯于各种事情那样；他不把它们理解为神圣的事情，而理解为平庸的事情，因为对神圣的事情并不存在习惯和依赖的关系。
他把按照一个民族、而且是斯巴达民族的法律来生活——其中恰恰有最高的必然性和伦理自由的最高能量——理解为一种偶然性和依赖，理解为某种平庸经验的东西，而这恰恰是最合乎理性的东西。
至于主观性的那种可怜相——援引精细的判断和知性，或者夸耀一种德性——本来就谈不上落到他们头上，而这种可怜相的阙如又太卑微，无法在他们身上被标举为德性。——更不用提在[雅可比的]《沃尔德马》里突出克莱奥墨涅斯的客观性了，因为这位斯巴达人在这里被引入，不是在他与自己祖国的关系中、在他真实德性的力量中，而是在他灭亡的个体性中；而且是为了让谁得到教化呢？——矫揉造作或无足轻重的女人和感伤的市民。

en: Otherwise, however, since for Jacobi ethical beauty is contrary to the concept and to objectivity, one can only hold to the figures in which he wanted to make his idea of ethical beauty clear.

But the fundamental tone of these figures is this conscious lack of objectivity, this subjectivity stuck fast to itself, the constant, not composure but reflection, upon one's own personality, this contemplation that eternally returns to the subject, which puts in the place of ethical freedom the utmost anxiousness, longing egoism and ethical sickliness, - a contemplating of oneself that performs with beautiful individuality precisely the transformation that took place with faith, namely through this consciousness of individual beauty to give oneself the consciousness of sublated subjectivity and of annihilated egoism, but through this consciousness to have posited precisely the highest subjectivity and inner idolatry, and at the same time to have justified them.

Just as we find the damnation of hell expressed in the poets who recognise what is eternal and what is finite and damned — in the ancients, in Dante, and in Goethe's Orestes, who in his life was for a time given over to hell — namely as the eternal being-bound to the subjective deed, the being-alone with one's own, with what belongs to oneself, and the immortal contemplation of this property, - so we see in the heroes Allwill and Woldemar211) this very torment of the eternal beholding of themselves, not even in a deed, but in the still greater boredom and powerlessness of empty being, and this fornication with oneself presented as the ground of the catastrophe of their un-novelistic events, but at the same time in the resolution this principle not sublated, and the un-catastrophising virtue of the whole circle of characters likewise essentially tinged with a more or less of that hell.
zh: 不过，既然在雅可比那里伦理的美与概念和客观性相抵触，人们就只好抓住那些他想借以讲清自己伦理的美之观念的形象。

但这些形象的基本音调，是这种有意识地缺乏客观性，是这种牢牢粘在自己身上的主观性，是这种持续不断的、不是沉着而是对自己人格的反思，是这种永远回到主体身上的考察——它用极度的局促不安、渴望式的自我主义和伦理上的病态，取代了伦理的自由；——这是一种对自己的考察，它对美的个体性所做的，正是信仰所经历的那种转变，即通过这种对个体美的意识而获得被扬弃的主观性和被消灭的自我主义的意识，但恰恰又通过这种意识设定了最高的主观性和内心的偶像崇拜，并同时为之作了辩护。

正如在那些认识到什么是永恒的、什么是有限的和被诅咒的诗人们那里——在古代人那里，在但丁那里，以及在歌德笔下那个生前曾一度被交给地狱的奥瑞斯特那里——我们看到地狱的诅咒被说了出来，即与主观的行为永远绑在一起，与自己的、属于自身的东西单独相处，以及对这份财产的永不停止的注视；——同样，在主人公阿尔维尔和沃尔德马211)身上，我们看到这种永远注视自己的痛苦，甚至不是在一桩行为中，而是在空虚存在的更大无聊和无力中，并且看到这种与自己的淫乱被表现为他们那些非小说式事件的灾难的根据，但同时在这种解决中这个原则并没有被扬弃，而周围所有性格的那种不制造灾难的德性，本质上也都染上了那种地狱的多多少少。

en: If, then, in Jacobi Protestant subjectivity seems to return out of the Kantian form of the concept to its true shape, a subjective beauty of feeling and of the lyric of heavenly longing, yet faith and individual beauty are, through the essential ingredient of reflection and of consciousness about this subjective beauty, thrown out of the unprejudicedness and unconstrainedness through which alone it is capable of being beautiful and pious and religious.
zh: 所以，如果说在雅可比那里，新教的主观性似乎从康德的概念形式返回到它真实的形态，即感受和天上渴望之抒情诗的主观的美，那么信仰和个体的美却由于反思以及对这种主观的美的意识这个本质成分，被抛出了那种无成见和无顾忌的状态——唯有在这种状态中，它才可能是美的、虔敬的和宗教的。

en: It follows, then, from what has gone before that the Kantian philosophy is opposed to the Jacobian, in so far as, within the sphere common to them, the Kantian sets absolute subjectivity and finitude in pure abstraction and thereby gains the objectivity and the infinity of the concept, whereas the Jacobian does not take finitude itself up into the concept but makes it, as finite finitude, as empirical contingency and consciousness of this subjectivity, into the principle.

The common sphere of both philosophies is the absolute being of the opposition between finitude, the natural, knowledge — but for that very reason a formal one — and the supernatural, supersensuousness and infinity; for both, therefore, the truly absolute is an absolute beyond in faith or in feeling and nothing for cognising reason.

In both the speculative idea occurs; in the Kantian philosophy it enters purely into the deduction of the categories, only to become at once a pure identity, a unity of the understanding, and otherwise counts as a merely possible thought that can win no reality in thinking, because reflection is supposed to be absolutely what rules; in Jacobi it is likewise present in subjective [form] as something particular, ingenious, which may just as little be taken up into universality as reason may become something seeing out of instinct and subjective individuality, namely something for thinking.
zh: 于是从前面所说的可以得出：康德哲学与雅可比哲学是对立的，因为在它们共同的领域内，康德哲学以纯粹抽象设定绝对的主观性和有限性，并由此获得概念的客观性和无限性，而雅可比哲学则根本不把有限性本身纳入概念，反而把它当作有限的有限性、当作经验的偶然性和这种主观性的意识，立为原则。
这两种哲学共同的领域，是有限性、自然的东西、知识——但正因如此是形式的东西——与超自然的东西、超感性的东西和无限性之间那种对立的绝对存在；所以对两者来说，真正的绝对者都是信仰或情感中的一个绝对的彼岸，对进行认识活动的理性来说则什么也不是。
在两者那里都出现了思辨的观念；在康德哲学中，它纯粹地进入范畴的演绎，但随即就变成一种纯粹的同一性、一种知性统一性，此外则被当作一个仅仅可能的想法，它在思维中不能获得任何实在性，因为反思应当绝对地占统治地位；在雅可比那里，它同样以主观的[形式]出现，是某种特殊的、机智的东西，它既不容被纳入普遍性，正如理性也不容从本能和主观的个体性出发去看，即不容成为思维的东西。

en: Because this side of the predominant subjective and finite, which is necessary once philosophy has taken its direction towards the form of reflection, is indeed also expressed by other philosophical endeavours, but partly more weakly, partly without this pretension, it could be presented with preference in the Jacobian form, which expresses theoretical and practical subjectivity as well as the beyond of faith most clearly, as in the representative of its kind.
At the same time, however, it is to be noted that this side itself can be grasped in a higher and nobler shape.

It has already been remarked that the principle of Jacobian philosophising, in that it raises the individual and particular above the concept and asserts subjective liveliness, approaches on the one hand the subjective beauty of Protestantism, which does not recognise the intercourse with God and the consciousness of the divine in the satiating objectivity of a cult and in the intrinsically clear and present intuition and enjoyment of this nature and this universe, but determines that intercourse and consciousness as an inner one that keeps the fixed form of an inner, and as a longing for a beyond and a future, - a longing that, although it cannot unite with its eternal object, has its beauty and its infinite enjoyment in this, that its object is truly and without wanting to keep anything of its own in reserve for itself the eternal; but on the other hand, through the Jacobian principle the beauty of individuality and its form of feeling and love and faith is clouded by the fact that faith, in so far as it bears on the eternal, has a polemical reference and thereby the insurmountable reflex of subjectivity, and is also extended as absolute certainty to the temporal and actual, so that the testimony of the senses counts as a revelation of truth and feeling and instinct contain the rule of ethical life, and that through reflection upon personality and upon the fact that man in general and the particular person is the subject of such beautiful feeling and love, the longing becomes a warming at its subjectivity, its beautiful thoughts and feelings.

But the truth that is in nature, in the form of actuality and temporality, and the consciousness [of the individual] of his absolute personality, cannot reconcile the pain of religious longing, nor call it back out of its beyond; for nature as temporal and the individual as something absolute in its singleness is not nature as the universe, in whose beholding as a this-worldly one the longing could find its peace, nor is the absoluteness of the subject in its personal singleness and permanent opposition to the eternal a reason that would be seeing, a love that would be pure, a faith that would be living, but if the temporal, subjective and empirical obtains truth and certainty for the longing, the beauty of its subjective nature, its faith, its love and its feeling in general have only been contaminated by such a reconciliation.
zh: 因为这种占优势的主观的、有限的东西这一面——一旦哲学把方向转向反思的形式，它就是必然的——虽然也被其他哲学努力所表达，但一部分表达得较弱，一部分并没有这种自负，所以这一面可以优先在雅可比的形式上得到展示，因为这种形式把理论的和实践的主观性以及信仰的彼岸说得最清楚，它就是这一类的代表。
但同时也要注意到，这一面本身可以被把握为一种更高贵、更崇高的形态。

前面已经提醒过：雅可比式哲学的原则，由于把个体的和特殊的东西抬高到概念之上并主张主观的生动性，一方面接近新教的主观的美——新教并不在一种崇拜的令人满足的客观性中、也不在对这个自然和这个宇宙的内在地清晰而当下在场的直观和享受中，认识与上帝的交往和对神性的意识，而是把那种交往和意识规定为一种内在的东西，它保持着内在之物的固定形式，并规定为对一种彼岸和一种未来的渴望；——这种渴望虽然不能与它永恒的对象结合，却在这一点上有它的美和它无限的享受，即它的对象真实地、并且不想在背地里为自己保留任何自己的东西地就是永恒的东西；但另一方面，雅可比的原则又使个体的美及其感受、爱和信仰的形式变得浑浊，因为信仰只要指向永恒的东西，就带有论战性的顾及，因而带有主观性那种不可克服的反射，而且作为绝对的确定性也被扩展到时间性的和现实的东西上，以致感官的见证被视为真理的启示，情感和本能包含着伦理的规则，并且由于对人格的反思，以及对人一般和这个特殊的人就是这样一种美的感受和爱的主体这一点的反思，渴望就变成对自身主观性、对自己美好的思想和感受的一种取暖。

但自然中的真理，以现实性和时间性的形式，以及[个体]对自己绝对人格的意识，都不能调解宗教渴望的痛苦，也不能把它从它的彼岸唤回来；因为作为时间性东西的自然和作为在其单一性中绝对者的个体，并不是作为宇宙的自然——在对宇宙的直观这种此岸的直观中，渴望本可以找到自己的安宁——；而主体在其个人单一性和对永恒东西的持久对立中的绝对性，也不是一种能看的理性、一种纯洁的爱、一种活生生的信仰，相反，如果时间性的、主观的和经验的东西对渴望来说获得了真理和确定性，那么它主观本性的美、它的信仰、它的爱和它的一般感受，就只是被这样一种调解弄脏了。

en: If, then, in the Jacobian principle the pain and the longing of Protestantism advance to a reconciliation, but in the manner of eudaimonism in general through something finite, initially through the reflection and the consciousness of the feeling and of the longing, which reflection and consciousness make the subject of the same as such into something, and if this longing finds the this-worldly in itself, in that it defiles itself with itself and holds the common actuality and temporality for revelation, then, thus reflected into itself, it could find a higher potency than Jacobi presented, create for the deification of the subject a higher object in it, and feeling as well as the intuition of itself and of the world could be grasped more ideally, which on the other side is just as much as making the highest intuition itself into something subjective and peculiarly permanent.

If the this-worldly, which has truth, instead of being actuality is the universe, and the reconciliation with nature is identity with the universe, as feeling infinite love, as intuition however religion, but in such a way that this identity itself, whether it be more than the passivity of apprehending and inner reproducing or more than virtuosity, is to remain something absolutely subjective and particular, is not to fix its utterance, nor entrust its liveliness to objectivity, and thereby is to retain precisely the former reflection of the longing upon the subject, then the Jacobian principle has reached the highest potentising of which it is capable, and Protestantism, which seeks reconciliation in the this-worldly, has driven itself to the highest point without stepping out of its character of subjectivity.
In the Speeches on Religion this potentising has taken place.

Since in the Jacobian philosophy reason is conceived only as instinct and feeling, and ethical life only in empirical contingency and as dependence on things as experience and inclination and the sense of the heart give them, while knowing is conceived only [as] a consciousness of particularities and peculiarity, whether outer or inner, so in these Speeches, by contrast, nature is annihilated as a collection of finite actualities and recognised as the universe, whereby the longing is brought back from its fleeing beyond actuality after an eternal beyond, the dividing wall between the subject or cognition and the absolute unattainable object is torn down, the pain is reconciled in enjoyment, and the endless striving is satisfied in beholding.

But while the individual thus throws its subjectivity off itself and the dogmatism of longing dissolves its opposition in idealism, this subject-objectivity of the intuition of the universe is nevertheless again to remain something particular and subjective; the virtuosity of the religious artist is to be allowed to mix its subjectivity into the tragic seriousness of religion, and instead of this individuality either concealing itself beneath the body of an objective presentation of great figures and their movement among one another, the movement of the universe, but in them - as in the triumphant church of nature genius edified itself in epics and tragedies - or instead of taking its subjective element away from the lyrical expression by the latter being at the same time present in memory and appearing as general speech, this subjective element is to constitute the essential liveliness and truth in the presentation of one's own intuition of the universe as well as in its production in others, art is to endure without a work of art, and the freedom of the highest intuition is to consist in singleness and in having something particular for oneself.

If the priest can only be a tool and servant, which offers itself up to the congregation and to itself and to it, in order to do what is limiting and objective in religious intuition, and to whom all power and strength before the mature congregation can belong only as to a representative, - then the congregation, presenting itself as immature, is to have the purpose and intention of letting the inner content of the intuition be brought about in itself by him as a virtuoso of edification and enthusiasm; to a subjective peculiarity of intuition (one is called idiot in so far as there is peculiarity in him), instead of annihilating it and at least not recognising it, so much is to be conceded that it forms the principle of a congregation of its own, and that in this way the little congregations and particularities assert and multiply themselves into the infinite, drift apart according to contingency and seek one another again, and at every moment change their groupings like the figures of a sea of sand abandoned to the play of the winds, while each of them at the same time, as is fair, holds the particularity of its view and its peculiarity to be something so idle and even disregarded that, indifferent to the recognition of the same, they renounce objectivity and in a general atomism can all quietly remain side by side, to which admittedly the enlightened separation of church and state fits very well, and in which idea an intuition of the universe cannot be an intuition of it as spirit, because what is spirit is not present as a universe in the state of atoms, and in general the catholicity of religion consists only in negativity and in the universality of being-singular.

If, then, the subjectivity of longing has already raised itself into the objectivity of beholding and the reconciliation takes place not with actuality but with the living, not with singleness but with the universe, then even this beholding of the universe is again made into subjectivity, in that it is partly virtuosity or not even a longing but only the seeking of a longing, partly it is not to constitute itself organically, nor is true virtuosity to obtain its objectivity and reality in laws and in the body of a people and of a general church, but the utterance is to be something absolutely inner, immediate outburst or imitation of individual and particular enthusiasm, and not the true utterance, a work of art, is to be present.
zh: 所以，如果在雅可比的原则中，新教的痛苦和渴望进展为一种调解，但却是以一般幸福论的方式、通过有限的东西，首先是通过对感受和渴望的反思和意识——这种反思和意识把感受和渴望的主体本身变成了某种东西——，并且如果这种渴望在自身中找到了此岸，因为它用自己弄脏自己，把平庸的现实性和时间性当成启示，那么，这样返回到自身之中的它，就可以找到比雅可比所展示的更高的级次，可以在它身上为对主体的神化造出更高的对象，并且感受以及对自己和世界的直观可以更观念地被把握，而这在另一方面就等于把最高的直观本身也变成某种主观的、独自持存的东西。

如果此岸——它有真理——不是现实性而是宇宙，与自然的调解就是与宇宙的同一性，作为感受是无限的爱，作为直观则是宗教，但却是这样：这种同一性本身，不论是作为比把握和内在摹写的被动性更多的东西，还是作为比高超技艺更多的东西，都应当始终是某种绝对主观的、特殊的东西，不应当把它的表达固定下来，也不应当把它的生动性托付给客观性，并因此恰好保留先前那种渴望对主体的反思，那么雅可比的原则就达到了它所能达到的最高级次提升，而在此岸中寻求调解的新教，也就把自己推到了最高点，却没有走出它主观性的性格。
在《论宗教》里，这种级次提升已经发生了。

由于在雅可比哲学中，理性只被理解为本能和情感，伦理只被理解为经验性的偶然性和对事物的依赖——事物是由经验、爱好和心意给出的——，而知识只被理解为对特殊性和独特性的意识，无论是外在的还是内在的，所以在《论宗教》里情况相反：自然作为有限现实性的集合被消灭，并被承认为宇宙，渴望因此从它越过现实性向永恒彼岸的逃遁中被召回，主体或认识与绝对而不可企及的客体之间的隔墙被拆除，痛苦在享受中得到调解，而无止境的追求则在观看中得到满足。

但是，当个体这样把自己的主观性从自己身上扔掉，渴望的独断论把自己的对立消解在观念论中时，这种对宇宙的直观的主体—客体性却又应当仍然是某种特殊的、主观的东西；宗教艺术家的高超技艺应当被允许把它的主观性掺进宗教的悲剧性严肃之中，并且，这种个体性不是要么隐藏在客观地展示伟大形象及其相互运动——即宇宙的运动，但却是在这些形象之中——的外壳之下（就像在自然的凯旋教会中，天才在史诗和悲剧中为自己造了居所），也不是要么以这样的办法从抒情表达中拿走它的主观东西，即让抒情表达同时存在于记忆中并作为一般的言说出场，相反，这种主观的东西应当在展示自己对宇宙的直观以及在他者身上产生这种直观时构成本质的生动性和真理，艺术应当没有艺术作品地延续下去，而最高直观的自由则应当存在于单一性和自为地拥有某种特殊东西之中。

如果说教士只能做一个工具和仆人，为教团、也为自身并向教团献出自己，去做宗教直观中限制性的、客观的东西，并且他作为代表，只有面对成熟的教团才能拥有全部权力和力量，——那么，教团把自己弄成未成年的，就该抱有这样的目的和意图：让直观的内在东西由他、由一位教化和激励方面的技艺大师在自身中产生出来；对直观的一种主观的独自性（一个人身上有独自性，就被叫作 Idiot），不是去消灭它、至少不是不承认它，而是要让步到这种程度，使它可以构成一个自己的教团的原则，并以这种方式使那些小教团和特殊性无限地为自己争得地位、不断繁殖，按偶然性各自漂散又彼此寻找，每一刻都像任凭风吹的沙海的图形那样改变组合，而同时，每一个这样的组合都很公道地把自己观点的特殊性和自己的独自性看作如此闲散、甚至无人理会的东西，以致它们对被人承认漠不关心，放弃客观性，在一种普遍的原子论中大家都能安静地并存；开明的政教分离当然非常合这个，而在这种观念中，对宇宙的直观不可能是把宇宙作为精神来直观，因为在原子的状态中，精神的东西并不作为宇宙存在，而且一般来说，宗教的大公性只在于否定性和单一存在的普遍性。

所以，如果说渴望的主观性已经把自己提升为观看的客观性，而调解不是与现实性、而是与活的东西、不是与单一性、而是与宇宙发生，那么，这种对宇宙的观看本身又被弄成了主观性：一方面，它是高超技艺，或者甚至不是一种渴望，而只是对一种渴望的寻找；另一方面，它不应当有机地把自己构成起来，真正的技艺也不应当在法律中、在一个民族和一种普遍教会的身体中获得自己的客观性和实在性，而表达应当是某种绝对内在的东西，是单个和特殊的热忱的直接爆发或模仿，并且不应当是真实的表达、不应当有艺术作品存在。
